sapphire.name: Sapphire
sapphire.definition: Corundum, aluminum oxide (Al2O3); every color but red is sapphire. Mohs 9. Bead grades: Sri Lanka, Madagascar, Tanzania (Umba, Songea), India, cut in Jaipur.
sapphire.judging: Under a 10x loupe, silk and angular zoning confirm natural corundum; a perfectly clean, uniform strand at $2/ct is glass or synthetic. Glass shows round bubbles; sapphire scratches a quartz bead.
sapphire.treatments: Heat is standard, permanent and needs no special care, so § 23.24 doesn't force disclosure, but the trade expects it. Beryllium diffusion, common in Songea oranges and yellows, affects value and must be disclosed under § 23.24(c). Tag line: "Natural sapphire, heated (standard, permanent treatment)." Songea: "Natural sapphire, heated; may be beryllium diffused." Write "unheated," "Ceylon" or "Umba" only when the invoice does (§ 23.1).
sapphire.care: Daily wear, ultrasonic fine. Store apart from softer stones.
sapphire.uses: Gold-fill fine-jewelry makers, bridal and birthstone sellers. 2 to 3mm rondelles on wire-wrapped chain are the volume item; pink briolettes for earrings.
sapphire.carried: Micro-faceted rondelles 2 to 4mm, pear briolettes, ovals, tumbled cubes. Retail per 8 inches, per 16.
talkingPoints: Same mineral as a $10,000 ring stone, cut small and strung.
Hardness 9: the strand her granddaughter will still wear.
sapphire.folklore: September birthstone; tradition links it to wisdom and loyalty (tradition, not fact).

ruby.name: Ruby
ruby.definition: Red corundum, Al2O3 colored by chromium, Mohs 9. Bead grades: India, Mozambique, Madagascar, Myanmar. Most cheap bright ruby beads are lead-glass-filled composites.
ruby.judging: Assume glass filling until proven otherwise. Under a loupe, filled fractures show a blue or orange flash as you tilt the bead, trapped gas bubbles, and dull glassy patches at the drill hole. Garnet stays dark under UV; ruby glows red.
ruby.treatments: Heat is normal and permanent. Lead-glass filling makes a composite, and § 23.25(d) says it's deceptive to call material with any glass filler "ruby," "treated ruby" or even "composite ruby" unless the term is qualified to disclose clearly that it (A) doesn't have the same characteristics as ruby and (B) requires special care. Tag line: "Composite ruby (lead-glass filled). Not the durability of natural ruby; special care required: no ultrasonic, steam, acids, household cleaners or jeweler's torch." Confirmed unfilled lots: "Natural ruby, heated."
ruby.care: Composite ruby is a hardness-9 skin over soft glass; lemon juice, bleach, jewelry dip and a torch etch it. Soft cloth only.
ruby.uses: Birthstone sellers, budget bridal, red accents in gold fill. 2mm spacers and teardrop earrings sell best.
ruby.carried: Shaded, commercial faceted rondelles 2 to 2.5mm and pear or teardrop drops,. Assume 8 to 15 ct per 8 inches. Retail per 8 inches, per 16.
talkingPoints: Ruby red at a garnet price, and here's exactly why.
I'll show you the glass under the loupe before you buy.
ruby.folklore: July birthstone; tradition ties it to passion (tradition, not fact).

emerald.name: Emerald
emerald.definition: Green beryl, Be3Al2Si6O18 colored by chromium and vanadium. Mohs 7.5 to 8 but brittle and usually fractured. Bead grades: Zambia, Brazil, lower-grade Colombian and Indian material.
emerald.disclosureLine: Natural emerald, clarity enhanced with oil (standard). Oil may dry out over time; no ultrasonic, steam or solvents.
emerald.judging: Judge color first: medium green that stays green in daylight, not gray or blackish, shaded evenly. The mossy "jardin" under a loupe confirms beryl. Dyed quartz pools green in cracks, glass has bubbles, aventurine glitters.
emerald.treatments: Nearly all emerald is oiled (cedar oil) or resin-filled to hide fractures. Oil dries out over years and dislikes heat and solvents, so § 23.24(a) and (b) require disclosure. Tag line: "Natural emerald, clarity enhanced with oil (standard). Oil may dry out over time; no ultrasonic, steam or solvents."
emerald.care: Warm water, mild soap, soft cloth. No ultrasonic, steam, jewelry dip or hot dashboards.
emerald.uses: Birthstone sellers, makers pairing green with yellow gold, layering designers. Rondelles are volume; hearts and pears are gifts.
emerald.carried: Shaded faceted rondelles 2.5 to 3mm at ; smooth hearts and pears online at a strand. Assume 10 to 15 ct per 8 inches. Retail per 8 inches, per 16.
talkingPoints: Zambian color at bead prices because the stone is small, not fake.
Every emerald on earth is oiled, Tiffany's included.
emerald.folklore: May birthstone; tradition ties it to rebirth and foresight (tradition, not fact).

tanzanite.name: Tanzanite
tanzanite.definition: Blue-violet zoisite, calcium aluminum silicate, Ca2Al3(SiO4)3(OH). Mohs 6 to 7 with one direction of perfect cleavage. One source on earth: the Merelani Hills near Arusha, Tanzania.
tanzanite.judging: Commercial tanzanite is light lavender to grayish blue, often cloudy; saturated blue-violet with a purple flash is better. Turn a bead: tanzanite shows blue one way and violet or bronze another. Iolite is harder, lighter, grayer, and swings from violet-blue to nearly colorless.
tanzanite.treatments: Nearly all tanzanite is heated to about 600 C to turn brown zoisite blue. Heat is permanent with no special care, so § 23.24 isn't triggered, but state it. Tag line: "Natural tanzanite, heated (standard, permanent treatment)." Don't sell iolite as "water sapphire" or "tanzanite color" (§ 23.26).
tanzanite.care: Necklaces and earrings, not bracelets or rings. No ultrasonic, steam or sudden temperature change.
tanzanite.uses: December birthstone sellers, designers who want violet-blue that isn't amethyst, wire-wrappers using 3 to 4mm accents.
tanzanite.carried: Faceted rondelles 3 to 5mm, pears, tubes, smooth ovals and nuggets at, commercial grade. Assume 35 ct per 8 inches at 4mm. Retail per 8 inches, per 16.
talkingPoints: One hill in Tanzania, and the mine is finite.
Look for the purple flash; iolite can't do that.
tanzanite.folklore: December birthstone (added 2002); Maasai tradition links blue with new birth (tradition, not fact).

ethiopian-welo-opal-white-and-crystal.name: Ethiopian Welo opal, white and crystal
ethiopian-welo-opal-white-and-crystal.definition: Hydrated silica, SiO2 with 3 to 10 percent water. Mohs 5.5 to 6.5. Mined in Wollo (Welo) province, Ethiopia, found 2008. Hydrophane: it soaks up water, turns temporarily clear, then dries back.
ethiopian-welo-opal-white-and-crystal.disclosureLine: Natural Ethiopian opal, untreated. Hydrophane: absorbs water, lotion and perfume, which can temporarily change its look. Keep dry.
ethiopian-welo-opal-white-and-crystal.origins: Hydrophane: it soaks up water, turns temporarily clear, then dries back
ethiopian-welo-opal-white-and-crystal.judging: Buy play-of-color: a good bead flashes green, orange and blue from several angles. Reject crazing (spidery cracks under a loupe). Opalite glass glows milky blue with no real flash; synthetic opal shows a too-regular "lizard skin" pattern. A water drop on Welo soaks in within a minute.
ethiopian-welo-opal-white-and-crystal.treatments: White and crystal Welo is normally untreated; dyed or resin-stabilized lots fall under § 23.24. Hydrophane behavior isn't a treatment, but print it. Tag line: "Natural Ethiopian opal, untreated. Hydrophane: absorbs water, lotion and perfume, which can temporarily change its look. Keep dry."
ethiopian-welo-opal-white-and-crystal.care: Remove for showers, swimming and lotion; if it clouds, let it dry a few days. No ultrasonic or heat.
ethiopian-welo-opal-white-and-crystal.uses: Etsy fine-jewelry makers, October birthstone sellers, boho and bridal designers. Drops for earrings and pendants are the profit item.
ethiopian-welo-opal-white-and-crystal.carried: Smooth rondelles 3 to 5mm, rounds, pear drops and nuggets at ; premium bright drops. Opal is light: assume 20 ct per 8 inches at 4mm. Retail per 8 inches, per 16.
talkingPoints: Every one of these flashes differently in your customer's light.
Real precious opal at a tenth of Australian prices; here's the care card.
ethiopian-welo-opal-white-and-crystal.folklore: October birthstone; tradition ties opal to hope (tradition, not fact).

black-ethiopian-opal-smoked.name: Black Ethiopian opal, smoked
black-ethiopian-opal-smoked.definition: The same Welo hydrophane opal, SiO2 with water, Mohs 5.5 to 6.5, with a gray to black body produced by smoking: paper-wrapped opal is heated so carbon lodges in its pores. Labs have found no naturally black Ethiopian opal; assume it's smoked.
black-ethiopian-opal-smoked.disclosureLine: implies natural Australian black (§ 23.26). Tag line: .
black-ethiopian-opal-smoked.judging: Judge the flash first. Under a loupe, smoked material shows dark concentrated near the surface and in cracks, sooty and uneven rather than the glassy black of Lightning Ridge. Faceting hides crazing, so check closely. Soaking lightens smoked material, which is the tell.
black-ethiopian-opal-smoked.treatments: Smoking isn't fully permanent and creates care needs, so § 23.24(a) and (b) require disclosure. Plain "black opal" implies natural Australian black (§ 23.26). Tag line: "Ethiopian opal, smoke treated to darken body color. Not permanent: soaking or cleaning can lighten it. Hydrophane; keep dry."
black-ethiopian-opal-smoked.care: No soaking, ultrasonic or oils; hot soapy water can pull carbon out over time.
black-ethiopian-opal-smoked.uses: Designers wanting the black-opal look in silver-priced pieces. 6mm faceted rondelles as focals, 4mm smooth for full strands.
black-ethiopian-opal-smoked.carried: Smooth and faceted rondelles 4 to 6mm at a flat. Assume 20 ct per 8 inches at 4mm, about 45 at 6mm. Retail per 8 inches, per 16.
talkingPoints: Black opal look for the price of a good agate.
I'll say it before you ask: this color is smoked.
black-ethiopian-opal-smoked.folklore: October birthstone; same opal traditions as above (tradition, not fact).

chocolate-and-brown-ethiopian-opal.name: Chocolate and brown Ethiopian opal
chocolate-and-brown-ethiopian-opal.definition: Hydrophane precious opal with a brown, tan or red-brown body, SiO2 with water, Mohs 5.5 to 6.5. Natural brown body color is typical of the older Shewa (Mezezo) deposit, found 1994, which crazes badly. Brown Welo also exists, some of it smoked.
chocolate-and-brown-ethiopian-opal.disclosureLine: Natural Ethiopian opal, brown body color, untreated. Hydrophane; keep dry.
chocolate-and-brown-ethiopian-opal.judging: Crazing is the risk: hold each strand to the light and look for a web of hairline cracks, especially in Shewa material. Uniform dark chocolate that lightens at the drill hole suggests smoking.
chocolate-and-brown-ethiopian-opal.treatments: If the supplier confirms natural body color, only the hydrophane warning is needed. If smoked, use the black opal line under § 23.24(a) and (b). Natural: "Natural Ethiopian opal, brown body color, untreated. Hydrophane; keep dry." Unsure: swap in "may be smoke treated."
chocolate-and-brown-ethiopian-opal.care: Same as white Welo: keep dry, no lotions, ultrasonic or heat.
chocolate-and-brown-ethiopian-opal.uses: Designers working in bronze, copper and oxidized silver, autumn collections. Rondelles as full strands.
chocolate-and-brown-ethiopian-opal.carried: Smooth rondelles; no tag price recorded on the 2026-09-04 visit. A realistic tag is. Assume 20 to 30 ct per 8 inches at 4 to 5mm. Retail estimate per 8 inches, per 16.
talkingPoints: Fire on a coffee-colored base that nobody's grandmother owned.
Warm-tone opal for the copper and bronze crowd.
chocolate-and-brown-ethiopian-opal.folklore: October birthstone; no separate tradition for the brown variety (tradition, not fact).

australian-opal-gray-body.name: Australian opal, gray body
australian-opal-gray-body.definition: Precious opal, SiO2 with about 6 percent water, Mohs 5.5 to 6.5, non-hydrophane and far more stable. Bead grades: Coober Pedy, Mintabie, Andamooka (light and gray bodies), Lightning Ridge (dark).
australian-opal-gray-body.judging: Count beads that flash versus gray potch; a good strand shows color on most beads. Check the side of each heishi disc for a straight seam or black backing, which means a doublet or triplet. A water drop sits on Australian opal instead of soaking in.
australian-opal-gray-body.treatments: Normally untreated. Andamooka matrix is sometimes sugar-acid darkened and needs disclosure under § 23.24(c). Doublets and triplets can't be sold as plain "opal" (§ 23.25). Tag line: "Natural Australian opal, solid, untreated."
australian-opal-gray-body.care: The most forgiving opal. Warm water and a soft cloth; avoid ultrasonic, dry heat and sudden temperature swings.
australian-opal-gray-body.uses: Designers who want "Australian" on the label. Heishi to boho and layered-necklace makers; faceted rondelles to wire-wrappers.
australian-opal-gray-body.carried: Heishi discs, faceted rondelles and smooth ovals with gray body and play-of-color at. Assume 20 to 30 ct per 8 inches. Retail per 8 inches, per 16.
talkingPoints: No water rules; this one you can forget you're wearing.
Gray body makes the color read in daylight.
australian-opal-gray-body.folklore: October birthstone; Australia's national gemstone since 1993 (fact); tradition links opal to hope (tradition, not fact).

tourmaline.name: Tourmaline
tourmaline.definition: Complex boron silicate; elbaite is the species behind pink, green and watermelon. Mohs 7 to 7.5, no cleavage, strongly pleochroic. Bead grades: Afghanistan, Nigeria, Brazil, Mozambique, Madagascar.
tourmaline.disclosureLine: Natural tourmaline. Pink may be heated or irradiated; both permanent, no special care.
tourmaline.judging: A good multi strand has clean pinks, greens and blues with few muddy brown-olive beads. Tourmaline is darker along the crystal's length than across it, and facet edges double under a loupe. Real watermelon slices show a rounded-triangular outline and a pink core grading to green rind; dyed agate slices show banding.
tourmaline.treatments: Some pink is heated or irradiated; both are permanent and need no special care, so § 23.24 isn't triggered. Tag line: "Natural tourmaline. Pink may be heated or irradiated; both permanent, no special care."
tourmaline.care: Fine for daily wear including bracelets; skip ultrasonic and steam on included beads and slices.
tourmaline.uses: Designers wanting color variety, October birthstone sellers, wire-wrappers. Multi rondelles are volume; slices and briolettes are high-ticket focals.
tourmaline.carried: Multi and watermelon faceted rondelles 2 to 4mm, tubes, cubes, pear briolettes, crystal sticks, heishi and slices at, fancy faceted, watermelon slices online at a strand; pink rondelles, ovals and pears ; green rondelles. Assume 17 ct per 8 inches at 3mm. Retail per 8 inches, per 16.
talkingPoints: Eleven colors, one mineral, one strand.
Sticks and slices are the crystal as it grew.
tourmaline.folklore: October birthstone (with opal); Egyptian legend has it passing through a rainbow (tradition, not fact).

london-blue-topaz.name: London blue topaz
london-blue-topaz.definition: Topaz, aluminum fluorosilicate, Al2SiO4(F,OH)2. Mohs 8 with one direction of perfect cleavage. "London blue" is a color name (deep steel blue with a green tint), not an origin. Colorless rough from Brazil, Sri Lanka and Nigeria is irradiated and heated.
london-blue-topaz.disclosureLine: Natural topaz, irradiated and heated to produce blue color (permanent). London blue is a color name, not an origin.
london-blue-topaz.judging: Real London blue is nearly always eye-clean, so judge depth of color (inky teal, not aqua) and facet sharpness. The threat is hydrothermal quartz in the same color, common in tubes. Weigh matching beads: topaz is about a third heavier than quartz.
london-blue-topaz.treatments: Irradiation plus heat defines the product. The color is permanent, but it transforms value versus untreated topaz, so disclose under § 23.24(c). US law also requires irradiated gemstones to pass through an NRC-licensed distributor who checks residual radioactivity. Tag line: "Natural topaz, irradiated and heated to produce blue color (permanent). London blue is a color name, not an origin." Hydro quartz can't be called topaz (§ 23.25(a)).
london-blue-topaz.care: Hard but cleavable: avoid sharp knocks and ultrasonic. Color is stable in sunlight.
london-blue-topaz.uses: Fine-jewelry designers wanting saturated blue without sapphire money, December birthstone sellers. Pears and marquise for earrings, melons as focals.
london-blue-topaz.carried: Faceted pears, marquise, tubes, carved melons, cubes, tyres and rondelles at. Assume 20 ct per 8 inches at 3mm, 35 at 4mm. Retail per 8 inches, per 16.
talkingPoints: The most saturated blue you can buy under $10 a carat.
Every London blue on earth is irradiated; the question is who says so.
london-blue-topaz.folklore: November birthstone (topaz), also listed for December as blue topaz; tradition ties it to calm (tradition, not fact).

swiss-blue-and-sky-blue-topaz.name: Swiss blue and sky blue topaz
swiss-blue-and-sky-blue-topaz.definition: The same topaz, Al2SiO4(F,OH)2, Mohs 8. Sky blue is a pale aquamarine-like blue; Swiss blue is bright electric blue. Both come from electron or gamma irradiation plus heat.
swiss-blue-and-sky-blue-topaz.disclosureLine: Natural topaz, irradiated and heated to produce blue color (permanent).
swiss-blue-and-sky-blue-topaz.judging: Eye-clean is normal, so judge evenness of color and crispness of faceting. Sky blue should have no gray; Swiss no green. Look-alikes are hydro quartz, glass and dyed quartz, all lighter in the hand, so the weight test applies.
swiss-blue-and-sky-blue-topaz.treatments: Irradiation and heat, permanent, no special care, but the treatment defines the product's value, so disclose under § 23.24(c). The NRC rule applies as for London blue. Tag line: "Natural topaz, irradiated and heated to produce blue color (permanent)."
swiss-blue-and-sky-blue-topaz.care: Warm soapy water; avoid hard knocks and ultrasonic on drilled beads. Color is stable.
swiss-blue-and-sky-blue-topaz.uses: Volume buyers making affordable "something blue" pieces, birthstone sellers. Coins and nuggets to statement designers; 4mm rondelles to everyone else.
swiss-blue-and-sky-blue-topaz.carried: Faceted rondelles, coins, nuggets and carved melons at. Assume 35 ct per 8 inches at 4mm; nuggets and melons run 80 to 120 ct. Retail per 8 inches, per 16; nugget strands.
talkingPoints: Cheaper than most quartz, and it's an 8 on the hardness scale.
Sky blue for the bride, Swiss blue for the bridesmaids.
swiss-blue-and-sky-blue-topaz.folklore: November birthstone (topaz), also listed for December as blue topaz; tradition associates it with calm (tradition, not fact).

natural-zircon.name: Natural zircon
natural-zircon.definition: Zirconium silicate, ZrSiO4, a natural mineral unrelated to cubic zirconia (ZrO2), a factory-grown diamond imitation. Mohs 6 to 7.5, brittle at facet edges, very dense, high fire. Brown and multi zircon comes from Tanzania, Sri Lanka and Madagascar; blue is heated Cambodian material.
natural-zircon.disclosureLine: Natural zircon (a natural mineral, not cubic zirconia), untreated.
natural-zircon.judging: Good natural zircon is lively: honey, cognac, red-brown, olive. Under a loupe, facet edges appear doubled, which single-refractive cubic zirconia never shows. Smoky quartz matches the color but is far lighter with no doubling.
natural-zircon.treatments: Brown and multi zircon is normally untreated; blue is heated, which is stable. Tag line: "Natural zircon (a natural mineral, not cubic zirconia), untreated." Selling CZ as "zircon" is deceptive under § 23.25(a).
natural-zircon.care: Necklaces and earrings; brittle edges make it a poor bracelet stone. Warm soapy water, no ultrasonic.
natural-zircon.uses: December birthstone sellers, designers pairing warm browns with gold, buyers who want fire without diamond prices. 3mm rondelles and briolettes sell best.
natural-zircon.carried: Faceted rondelles 3 to 4mm, pear briolettes and smooth ovals in multi and brown at. Zircon is heavy: assume 26 ct per 8 inches at 3mm, 48 at 4mm. Retail per 8 inches, per 16.
talkingPoints: This is the real December birthstone, and it's not CZ.
More fire than any other brown stone at the show.
natural-zircon.folklore: December birthstone; tradition credits it with sound sleep and prosperity (tradition, not fact).

sphene.name: Sphene
sphene.definition: Calcium titanium silicate, CaTiSiO5. Mohs 5 to 5.5 with cleavage, so a collector's gem, not a ring stone. Its dispersion (0.051) beats diamond's (0.044), so clean pieces throw real fire. Gem material: Madagascar, Pakistan (Skardu), Sri Lanka, Brazil, Mexico.
sphene.disclosureLine: Natural sphene (titanite), untreated. Soft stone; see care.
sphene.judging: Color runs yellow-green, olive and brownish green; greener and more transparent is better. Transparent ovals show fire even polished smooth. Under a loupe, sphene shows very strong doubling and near-adamantine luster. Peridot is the closest color match but is harder, oily-looking and has no fire.
sphene.treatments: None known in the trade. Tag line: "Natural sphene (titanite), untreated. Soft stone; see care."
sphene.care: Pendants and earrings only. No ultrasonic, steam or bracelets. Store alone in a soft pouch; other beads will scratch it.
sphene.uses: Collectors, gemologists, designers who want a stone nobody else at the show can name. Ovals as pendant focals.
sphene.carried: Smooth ovals, one 950 ct lot at. Beads are rare; the rough is small and fragile. Assume 45 to 60 ct per 8 inches for 6x8 to 8x10mm ovals, so the lot is roughly 16 to 20 8-inch strands. Retail per 8 inches, per 16.
talkingPoints: More fire than diamond; hold it under the lamp and watch.
You will not find another tray of sphene beads at this show.
sphene.folklore: No birthstone and no long tradition; modern crystal lore only (tradition, not fact).

kunzite.name: Kunzite
kunzite.definition: Pink to lilac spodumene, lithium aluminum silicate, LiAlSi2O6, colored by manganese. Mohs 6.5 to 7 with perfect cleavage in two directions. Bead-grade rough: Afghanistan, Pakistan, Brazil, Madagascar.
kunzite.disclosureLine: Natural kunzite. Color fades with prolonged sunlight or heat; store in the dark. May be irradiated; ask for lot details.
kunzite.judging: Kunzite is pale, so bigger beads show more color; 4mm rondelles look like glass. Turn a bead and it shifts pink, violet and near colorless. Rose quartz is cloudier with no color shift. Reject beads with cleavage planes reaching the drill hole.
kunzite.treatments: Usually untreated, but some kunzite is irradiated to deepen the pink and that color is unstable, so § 23.24(a) requires disclosure when known. Even natural color fades in strong sunlight and heat. Tag line: "Natural kunzite. Color fades with prolonged sunlight or heat; store in the dark. May be irradiated; ask for lot details."
kunzite.care: Not a beach or windowsill stone; no ultrasonic, steam, hot water, halogen lamps or bracelets.
kunzite.uses: Bridal and blush-palette designers, statement makers who want big pale beads. Melons as focal runs; tubes for bar pendants.
kunzite.carried: Carved melons 8 to 10mm, smooth nuggets, tubes and ovals at. Melons are heavy: assume 90 to 150 ct per 8 inches, retail ; nugget and tube strands run 50 to 80 ct, retail.
talkingPoints: Ten millimeters of real pink gemstone at glass-melon prices.
Sell it with the care card; buyers respect hearing about fading first.
kunzite.folklore: No birthstone; modern crystal lore calls it a stone of emotional healing (tradition, not fact).

chrome-diopside.name: Chrome diopside
chrome-diopside.definition: Chromium-bearing diopside, calcium magnesium silicate, CaMgSi2O6. Mohs 5 to 6 with two directions of cleavage. Nearly all gem material comes from the Inagli deposit in Yakutia (Sakha), eastern Siberia, mined only in the short summer.
chrome-diopside.disclosureLine: Natural chrome diopside, untreated. Soft stone; see care.
chrome-diopside.judging: Bright grass green is ideal; the stone goes near black above about 5mm, so 3mm is the right size. Look for eye-clean beads with doubled facet edges under a loupe. Green glass has bubbles and no doubling; peridot is yellower and oily. Don't call it "Siberian emerald," a misleading varietal name under § 23.26.
chrome-diopside.treatments: None known. Tag line: "Natural chrome diopside, untreated. Soft stone; see care."
chrome-diopside.care: Earrings and necklaces, not bracelets or rings. No ultrasonic or steam. Store apart from harder beads.
chrome-diopside.uses: Designers who want emerald green in silver at a low ticket, May birthstone sellers offering an alternative. Accent runs of 3mm rondelles between pearls sell best.
chrome-diopside.carried: Faceted rondelles 3mm; no tag price recorded on the 2026-09-04 visit. Typical Jaipur wholesale for this cut is. Assume 18 ct per 8 inches. Retail estimate per 8 inches, per 16.
talkingPoints: Emerald green from Siberia, mined three months a year.
At 3mm it glows; that's the size to buy.
chrome-diopside.folklore: No birthstone; modern crystal lore only (tradition, not fact).

aquamarine.name: Aquamarine
aquamarine.definition: Blue to green-blue beryl (beryllium aluminum silicate) colored by iron. Mohs 7.5 to 8. Bead rough: Brazil, Nigeria, Mozambique, Pakistan.
aquamarine.disclosureLine: Natural aquamarine (beryl). May be heated; permanent.
aquamarine.judging: Even medium blue with no gray beats pale; moss inclusions should be spread evenly. Look-alikes: blue topaz (heavier, more saturated) and glass (round bubbles).
aquamarine.treatments: Most blue aquamarine is heated to remove green; permanent and undetectable, so 16 CFR 23.24 does not force disclosure. Say it anyway: "Natural aquamarine (beryl). May be heated; permanent." Multi-beryl: "Natural beryl mix (aquamarine, morganite, heliodor). May be heated."
aquamarine.care: Daily-wear durable. Warm soapy water; ultrasonic safe except on moss.
aquamarine.uses: Bridal and March-birthday work; moss and milky feed boho and beach designs. Rondelles and briolettes sell best.
aquamarine.carried: Clean blue : faceted rondelle 4 to 6mm, pear and heart briolette, heishi, tube, smooth oval, nugget. Milky : smooth oval, nugget, faceted pear, marquise, rectangle. Moss, teal to green, included: faceted rondelle 3 to 6mm, heishi, pear, heart, oval. Multi-beryl : rondelle, nugget, oval, tube, pear. Retail per 16 inches : clean blue milky moss multi-beryl ; half for 8.
talkingPoints: Same mineral as emerald, fraction of the price.
Moss is aquamarine with its geology left in.
aquamarine.folklore: March birthstone; by tradition a sailor's stone.

morganite.name: Morganite
morganite.definition: Pink to peach beryl colored by manganese; same family and chemistry as aquamarine, Mohs 7.5 to 8. Bead rough: Brazil, Mozambique, Nigeria.
morganite.disclosureLine: Natural morganite (pink beryl). Routinely heated to improve color; permanent.
morganite.judging: Pale by nature; "good" is soft peach-pink with real transparency and glassy luster. The usual confusion is rose quartz: cheaper, cloudier, pinker, and hazy throughout under a loupe, where morganite has clear windows and sharper facets.
morganite.treatments: Nearly all morganite is heated to remove orange; some is irradiated, then heated. Both permanent and undetectable, so 16 CFR 23.24 does not require disclosure; the trade norm is to state it. Tag: "Natural morganite (pink beryl). Routinely heated to improve color; permanent." Never "pink emerald" (16 CFR 23.26).
morganite.care: Daily-wear durable. Warm soapy water; ultrasonic usually safe. Strong sun can lighten it.
morganite.uses: Bridal and blush palettes with rose gold; a step-up from rose quartz. 6mm rondelles and tubes for bracelets.
morganite.carried: Smooth tube and faceted rondelle 6mm;. Retail: per 16 inches, per 8.
talkingPoints: Beryl family, so it wears like aquamarine, not quartz.
Hold it next to rose quartz; the glassiness is the price difference.
morganite.folklore: No birthstone month; by tradition linked to compassion.

amethyst.name: Amethyst
amethyst.definition: Purple quartz colored by iron plus natural irradiation. Mohs 7. Bead material: Brazil and Uruguay for volume, Zambia for deep "African" grades.
amethyst.judging: Medium to dark purple with red or blue flash is the top; pale, zoned or brownish the bottom. Zambian is darker and more included, but in small rondelles inclusions vanish. Look-alikes: glass (bubbles, no color banding), purple fluorite (Mohs 4, a steel pin scratches it).
amethyst.treatments: Usually untreated; dye and fracture filling are rare. Tag: "Natural amethyst (quartz). Untreated." If dyed, 16 CFR 23.24 requires: "Amethyst, dyed; avoid solvents."
amethyst.care: Everyday durable. Warm soapy water; ultrasonic usually safe; no steam. Direct sun can fade it.
amethyst.uses: The February birthstone workhorse for earrings, bracelet stacks and mixed strands. Small rondelles sell best; pears for earrings.
amethyst.carried: Faceted rondelle 3 to 4mm, oval, tube, nugget, pear and heart, including dark African;. Retail: per 16 inches, half for 8.
talkingPoints: African amethyst is the grade jewelers pay extra for, cut small to hide inclusions.
Hold it to the light for the red flash.
amethyst.folklore: February birthstone; by tradition a sobriety stone (Greek amethystos, "not drunk").

pink-amethyst-and-rose-de-france.name: Pink amethyst and Rose de France
pink-amethyst-and-rose-de-france.definition: Two pale amethyst lines. Rose de France is a trade name for pale lilac to lavender amethyst, mainly Brazilian. Pink amethyst is a newer name for pinkish-lavender quartz from Patagonia, Argentina, tinted by hematite inclusions. Both quartz, Mohs 7.
pink-amethyst-and-rose-de-france.disclosureLine: Natural amethyst (quartz), pale lavender grade sold as Rose de France. Untreated.
pink-amethyst-and-rose-de-france.judging: Color is meant to be soft, so judge evenness and clarity: consistent lilac, eye-clean, crisp facets. Pink amethyst shows faint red-brown hematite dusting under a loupe; dyed quartz pools color in cracks and drill holes.
pink-amethyst-and-rose-de-france.treatments: Normally untreated. Tags: "Natural amethyst (quartz), pale lavender grade sold as Rose de France. Untreated." "Natural pink amethyst (quartz with hematite inclusions), Argentina. Untreated." Never "rose quartz" (16 CFR 23.26, varietal names).
pink-amethyst-and-rose-de-france.care: Everyday durable. Warm soapy water; ultrasonic usually safe. Avoid strong sun.
pink-amethyst-and-rose-de-france.uses: Pastel and bridal palettes with rose quartz, moonstone and pearl. Nuggets for statement necklaces; rondelles as spacers.
pink-amethyst-and-rose-de-france.carried: Faceted step-cut nugget and rondelle;. Retail: per 16 inches, half for 8.
talkingPoints: Rose de France is real amethyst; the name describes the shade.
Pink amethyst is from one Patagonian deposit; the pink is hematite, not dye.
pink-amethyst-and-rose-de-france.folklore: February birthstone by association; tradition attaches calm to pale shades.

ametrine.name: Ametrine
ametrine.definition: Bicolor quartz, amethyst purple and citrine yellow in one crystal (iron in two oxidation states), Mohs 7. Nearly all natural ametrine comes from one mine, Anahí, in Bolivia.
ametrine.disclosureLine: is partially heated amethyst, and synthetics exist. At $0.37/ct, assume treatment unless the supplier confirms Anahí origin. Tags: .
ametrine.judging: Both colors clearly present on most beads with a sharp boundary; muddy tan-purple is the low grade. Look-alikes: partially heated amethyst (diffuse, patchy zoning), hydrothermal synthetic (too clean, sometimes green-yellow), glass (bubbles).
ametrine.treatments: Bolivian ametrine is sold as natural, but much cheap "ametrine" is partially heated amethyst, and synthetics exist. At $0.37/ct, assume treatment unless the supplier confirms Anahí origin. Tags: "Natural ametrine (bicolor quartz), Bolivia. Untreated." or "Ametrine (bicolor quartz). May be heated; permanent." Synthetic must be labeled "laboratory-grown" (16 CFR 23.25).
ametrine.care: Everyday durable. Warm soapy water; ultrasonic usually safe. Avoid heat.
ametrine.uses: Two-tone designs without mixing strands; autumn and jewel-tone palettes. Step-cut nuggets are the shape people buy.
ametrine.carried: Faceted step-cut nugget and smooth oval;. Retail: per 16 inches, half for 8.
talkingPoints: Two gemstones in one crystal, from essentially one mine on earth.
Turn the bead and watch purple and gold switch.
ametrine.folklore: No birthstone; tradition treats it as amethyst calm plus citrine energy.

prasiolite.name: Prasiolite
prasiolite.definition: Green quartz, Mohs 7. Nearly all commercial prasiolite is amethyst from the Montezuma deposit, Minas Gerais, Brazil, heated to about 500 C; natural green quartz (Poland) is not what the bead trade sells.
prasiolite.judging: Pale, clean, slightly yellowish green with good transparency is correct; vivid or bottle-green is suspect. Look-alikes: hydrothermal "hydro" quartz and glass (both too even and clean; glass shows round bubbles), green fluorite (Mohs 4).
prasiolite.treatments: Heated by definition. Color is stable in wear but fades above about 150 C, so 16 CFR 23.24 applies (special care), and 16 CFR 23.26(b)(2) names "green amethyst" an incorrect varietal name. Tag: "Prasiolite (green quartz). Heat-treated amethyst; stable in normal wear, keep from high heat." Use "green amethyst" only in keywords, corrected.
prasiolite.care: Everyday durable. Warm soapy water; ultrasonic usually safe. No steam or torch nearby.
prasiolite.uses: Spring palettes and "peridot without the price" designs. Long ovals for stations; melons for statements.
prasiolite.carried: Faceted long oval and carved melon;. Retail: per 16 inches, half for 8.
talkingPoints: It is heated amethyst; every reputable dealer's is.
Soft mint is the real thing; neon green is glass.
prasiolite.folklore: No birthstone; tradition borrows amethyst's calm.

citrine-and-lemon-quartz.name: Citrine and lemon quartz
citrine-and-lemon-quartz.definition: Yellow to orange-brown quartz, Mohs 7. Natural citrine is uncommon; most commercial citrine, including orange "Madeira", is heated Brazilian amethyst. Lemon quartz is colorless quartz irradiated, then heated, to greenish-yellow.
citrine-and-lemon-quartz.disclosureLine: Citrine (quartz). Color produced by heating amethyst; permanent.
citrine-and-lemon-quartz.judging: Madeira should be saturated orange-brown with no muddy zones; lemon a clean, cool yellow. Heated amethyst often shows whitish zones near bead ends. Look-alikes: glass (bubbles), yellow fluorite (soft).
citrine-and-lemon-quartz.treatments: Heat and irradiation are permanent and stable, so 16 CFR 23.24 does not strictly require disclosure; the general deception rule (23.1) and customers do. Tags: "Citrine (quartz). Color produced by heating amethyst; permanent." "Lemon quartz. Irradiated and heated quartz; permanent, no residual radioactivity." Never "topaz" (16 CFR 23.25).
citrine-and-lemon-quartz.care: Everyday durable. Warm soapy water; ultrasonic usually safe. Lemon quartz can fade in prolonged sun.
citrine-and-lemon-quartz.uses: November-birthstone work, autumn palettes, lemon quartz for summer brights. Rondelles and briolettes.
citrine-and-lemon-quartz.carried: Faceted rondelle 3 to 4mm and pear briolette in shaded/Madeira citrine and lemon quartz;. Retail: rondelles per 16 inches, per 8; briolettes about per 8. The tag is top-of-market; the color must earn it.
talkingPoints: Almost every citrine started as amethyst; the tag says so.
Lemon quartz is the one clean lemon-yellow at this price.
citrine-and-lemon-quartz.folklore: November birthstone; by tradition the "merchant's stone".

rose-quartz.name: Rose quartz
rose-quartz.definition: Translucent pink quartz, Mohs 7, colored by microscopic fibers of a pink dumortierite-type mineral, which is why it is always hazy. Sources: Brazil, Madagascar, South Africa, India.
rose-quartz.judging: Even medium pink with a soft glow and no gray or brown; chalky white is the low grade. Look-alikes: dyed quartzite (color pooled in cracks and drill holes), glass (bubbles, perfectly clear). A transparent pink bead at this price is not rose quartz.
rose-quartz.treatments: Normally untreated. Pale material is sometimes dyed, which 16 CFR 23.24 requires disclosing. Tag: "Natural rose quartz. Untreated." If dyed: "Rose quartz, dyed; avoid solvents."
rose-quartz.care: Everyday durable. Warm soapy water; ultrasonic fine. Years of direct sun can fade it.
rose-quartz.uses: Entry-price pink for bracelet stacks, gift lines, bulk stringing. 3 to 4mm rondelles as spacers and full strands.
rose-quartz.carried: Faceted rondelle 3 to 4mm;. Retail: per 16 inches, per 8.
talkingPoints: The honest pink; the haze is the mineral, not a flaw.
Buy three strands and match the pinks.
rose-quartz.folklore: No birthstone; by long tradition the love and self-compassion stone.

smoky-and-cognac-quartz.name: Smoky and cognac quartz
smoky-and-cognac-quartz.definition: Brown quartz, Mohs 7, colored by natural radiation acting on trace aluminum. "Cognac quartz" is a bead-trade name for warm golden-brown smoky quartz, not a separate variety. Sources: Brazil, Madagascar, Colorado.
smoky-and-cognac-quartz.disclosureLine: Smoky quartz. Natural or irradiated; color is permanent.
smoky-and-cognac-quartz.judging: Clear brown you can read through, even bead to bead. Dead-uniform near-black with no zoning points to irradiation. Look-alikes: glass (bubbles), brown obsidian (shell-like chips, no zoning).
smoky-and-cognac-quartz.treatments: Much commercial smoky quartz is irradiated colorless quartz, heated to tune the shade. Permanent, stable and safe, so 16 CFR 23.24 does not require disclosure, but state it. Tags: "Smoky quartz. Natural or irradiated; color is permanent." "Cognac quartz (trade name for warm-brown smoky quartz). May be irradiated; permanent."
smoky-and-cognac-quartz.care: Everyday durable. Warm soapy water; ultrasonic fine. Strong heat can lighten it.
smoky-and-cognac-quartz.uses: Neutral, earthy palettes, men's bracelets, autumn lines; a cheap partner for citrine. Smooth rondelles and heishi.
smoky-and-cognac-quartz.carried: Smooth rondelle and faceted heishi. No tag observed; bead-market wholesale roughly. Retail: about per 16 inches, half for 8.
talkingPoints: A brown that goes with everything for almost nothing.
Cognac is the warm end of smoky; tone, not rarity.
smoky-and-cognac-quartz.folklore: No birthstone; tradition calls it a grounding stone.

crystal-quartz-and-golden-rutilated-quar.name: Crystal quartz and golden rutilated quartz
crystal-quartz-and-golden-rutilated-quar.definition: Colorless quartz (rock crystal), Mohs 7; rutilated quartz is rock crystal shot through with golden rutile (titanium dioxide) needles. Rock crystal: Brazil, Madagascar, India; golden rutilated: nearly all Brazilian. "Herkimer diamond" properly means double-terminated quartz from Herkimer County, New York; anything else is "Herkimer-style".
crystal-quartz-and-golden-rutilated-quar.judging: Rutilated: dense, bright gold needles evenly spread; sparse brown needles are lower grade. Look-alikes: glass (round bubbles, swirl marks, warms in the hand; quartz stays cold) and "hydro" synthetic quartz (flawless).
crystal-quartz-and-golden-rutilated-quar.treatments: Normally untreated; watch for coated ("aura") quartz and glass. Tags: "Natural rock crystal quartz. Untreated." "Natural golden rutilated quartz, Brazil. Untreated." Points: "Double-terminated quartz points, Herkimer-style (not from Herkimer County, NY)."
crystal-quartz-and-golden-rutilated-quar.care: Everyday durable. Warm soapy water; ultrasonic fine. Surface-reaching rutile can chip at drill holes.
crystal-quartz-and-golden-rutilated-quar.uses: Crystal is the universal spacer and "diamond look" filler; rutilated is a neutral with drama. Tubes and pears for earrings; points for pendants.
crystal-quartz-and-golden-rutilated-quar.carried: Faceted pear, rondelle, tube, Herkimer-style nuggets. No tag observed; market wholesale roughly for crystal, for rutilated. Retail: crystal per 16 inches ; rutilated pears per 8, rondelles per 16.
talkingPoints: Rutilated quartz is the only stone where the inclusions are the point.
Cold to the touch means quartz; glass warms fast.
crystal-quartz-and-golden-rutilated-quar.folklore: No birthstone; tradition calls rock crystal the "master healer".

strawberry-quartz-and-red-aventurine.name: Strawberry quartz and red aventurine
strawberry-quartz-and-red-aventurine.definition: Two materials, one loose name. Strawberry quartz: translucent quartz with red hematite inclusions (often mislabeled "lepidocrocite"), Mohs 7. Red aventurine: quartzite colored by hematite and mica, faint sparkle, Mohs 6.5 to 7. Sources are inconsistently reported; India supplies most aventurine.
strawberry-quartz-and-red-aventurine.disclosureLine: Natural strawberry quartz (quartz with hematite inclusions). Untreated.
strawberry-quartz-and-red-aventurine.judging: Strawberry quartz: translucent body with visible red flecks or needles. Red aventurine: opaque brick-red with faint glitter. The imitation is "cherry quartz", glass with swirled red streaks: under a loupe, round bubbles and smooth flowing swirls.
strawberry-quartz-and-red-aventurine.treatments: Both normally untreated. Tags: "Natural strawberry quartz (quartz with hematite inclusions). Untreated." "Natural red aventurine (quartzite). Untreated." Glass must carry "imitation" under 16 CFR 23.25(b): "Cherry quartz, imitation (glass)."
strawberry-quartz-and-red-aventurine.care: Everyday durable. Warm soapy water; ultrasonic fine. Aventurine is slightly porous; no harsh cleaners.
strawberry-quartz-and-red-aventurine.uses: Pink and red bracelet stacks, Valentine's lines. Heishi and rondelles as spacers; pears for earrings.
strawberry-quartz-and-red-aventurine.carried: Faceted pear, heishi, rondelle, tumbled nugget;, the low end almost certainly aventurine. Retail: per 16 inches, per 8.
talkingPoints: The red is hematite that grew inside the crystal, not dye.
Cherry quartz is glass; this is not.
strawberry-quartz-and-red-aventurine.folklore: No birthstone; tradition ties both to love and vitality.

rainbow-moonstone.name: Rainbow moonstone
rainbow-moonstone.definition: White labradorite, a plagioclase feldspar (sodium calcium aluminum silicate), not orthoclase moonstone; the blue or multicolor sheen is light scattering off thin internal layers. Mohs 6 to 6.5, perfect cleavage. Bead rough: mostly India.
rainbow-moonstone.disclosureLine: Natural rainbow moonstone (white labradorite feldspar). Untreated.
rainbow-moonstone.judging: Strong blue flash across most beads is the top grade; a few blue beads and the rest chalky is the bottom. Look-alike: opalite, a milky glass that glows the same from every angle and shows bubbles; feldspar sheen switches off as you tilt.
rainbow-moonstone.treatments: Untreated. Tag: "Natural rainbow moonstone (white labradorite feldspar). Untreated." Keep "labradorite" on the tag rather than relying on a trade name alone (16 CFR 23.26).
rainbow-moonstone.care: Earrings and necklaces, not rough-wear bracelets; hard knocks split it. Warm soapy water only; no ultrasonic or steam.
rainbow-moonstone.uses: Bridal, June-birthday, celestial and boho designers. Rondelles and briolettes move fastest; coins and cushions for statements.
rainbow-moonstone.carried: His biggest category by tray count. Pear and heart briolette, coin, oval, faceted rondelle 3 to 4mm, smooth nugget, cushion;. Retail: rondelles per 16 inches ; briolettes per 8 ; coins and nuggets per 16 ; half for 8.
talkingPoints: Roll it under the light and find the blue.
It is white labradorite, so it flashes harder than classic moonstone.
rainbow-moonstone.folklore: June birthstone; by tradition new beginnings.

peach-gray-chocolate-and-golden-shine-mo.name: Peach, gray, chocolate and golden-shine moonstone
peach-gray-chocolate-and-golden-shine-mo.definition: The orthoclase moonstones: potassium feldspar with thin albite layers that scatter light into a soft glow. (K,Na)AlSi3O8, Mohs 6 to 6.5, two cleavage directions. Body color from trace iron. Sources: nearly all India.
peach-gray-chocolate-and-golden-shine-mo.disclosureLine: Natural peach moonstone (orthoclase feldspar), India. Untreated.
peach-gray-chocolate-and-golden-shine-mo.judging: Clean body color with a visible moving sheen when tilted; flat beads with no glow are low grade. Look-alikes: opalite glass (uniform glow, bubbles), sunstone sold as peach moonstone (sunstone glitters, moonstone glows).
peach-gray-chocolate-and-golden-shine-mo.treatments: Untreated. Tag: "Natural peach moonstone (orthoclase feldspar), India. Untreated." Swap the color word as needed.
peach-gray-chocolate-and-golden-shine-mo.care: Earrings and pendants; cleavage makes it chip, so avoid rings. Warm soapy water only; no ultrasonic, steam or sudden heat.
peach-gray-chocolate-and-golden-shine-mo.uses: Neutral and earth-tone designers, bridal in peach, minimalist gray for silver work. Pears and marquise for earrings; heishi for bracelets.
peach-gray-chocolate-and-golden-shine-mo.carried: Faceted pear, marquise, rectangle, heishi. Top online sellers: peach 20 SKUs, gray 18. No tag observed; bead-market wholesale roughly. Retail: pears and marquise per 8 inches ; heishi per 16.
talkingPoints: Same mineral as classic moonstone, with color in the body.
Gray moonstone reads like smoke in silver; nothing else at this price does.
peach-gray-chocolate-and-golden-shine-mo.folklore: June birthstone; by tradition the stone of the moon and calm.

labradorite.name: Labradorite
labradorite.definition: Plagioclase feldspar (sodium calcium aluminum silicate), Mohs 6 to 6.5, perfect cleavage. The flash (labradorescence) is light reflecting off thin twin layers inside a gray to black body. Bead rough is mostly Madagascan.
labradorite.judging: Blue over most of the bead is standard "AA"; gold, green and purple alongside blue is "AAA" at about double. Look-alikes: foil-backed glass (bubbles, flash from one flat plane), coated feldspar (color at drill holes).
labradorite.treatments: Untreated. Tag: "Natural labradorite (feldspar), Madagascar. Untreated." Never "black moonstone" (16 CFR 23.26).
labradorite.care: Earrings, pendants and loose necklaces; hard knocks cleave it; big nuggets chip at the edges. Warm soapy water only; no ultrasonic or steam.
labradorite.uses: The gray-with-fire neutral for silver and boho work. Daggers and pears for earrings; nuggets and rectangles for statement necklaces.
labradorite.carried: Faceted pear, dagger, rectangle, rondelle, coin, flat nugget, statement pieces to 35mm;, tags inverse to size. Retail: rondelles per 16 inches, half for 8; statement strands per 8.
talkingPoints: Every bead is a different flash; no two strands match.
The stone people cross the aisle for.
labradorite.folklore: No birthstone; tradition calls it a stone of transformation.

gray-silverite.name: Gray silverite
gray-silverite.definition: A trade name, not a mineral, for gray to white labradorite or moonstone beads with a thin metallic or pearlescent coating giving a silver-blue sheen. Gemologists testing several sellers' silverite in 2015 found coated glass, and GIA does not recognize the name; the base varies by supplier.
gray-silverite.judging: Prove the base. Feldspar shows flat parallel cleavage planes and sheen from inside; glass shows round bubbles and surface-only sheen. At drill holes and chips the coating stops, exposing a different body color.
gray-silverite.treatments: Coated by definition; coatings are not permanent and need special care, so 16 CFR 23.24 requires disclosure, online included. Glass base: 16 CFR 23.25(b) requires "imitation" and 23.27 bars "natural". Tag (feldspar base): "Silverite is a trade name: labradorite/moonstone feldspar with a thin surface coating. Not permanent; avoid abrasives, ultrasonics and chemicals." Unconfirmed: "Silverite (trade name), coated bead; base unverified."
gray-silverite.care: Fragile. Soft damp cloth only; no ultrasonic, steam or solvents.
gray-silverite.uses: Shimmery gray for evening and bridal work below pearl prices. Faceted pears and rondelles.
gray-silverite.carried: Smooth oval, faceted pear, rondelle, heishi; ; 15 SKUs online. Retail: rondelles per 16 inches ; pears and ovals per 8.
talkingPoints: Coated feldspar; the flash is a finish, and here is how to keep it.
A gemstone with a manicure.

sunstone.name: Sunstone
sunstone.definition: Feldspar with aventurescence, a glittery copper-red sparkle from tiny flat platelets of hematite or copper. Bead-grade sunstone is oligoclase or orthoclase feldspar from Tamil Nadu, India, and Tanzania; Oregon is a different price tier. Mohs 6 to 6.5, two cleavage directions.
sunstone.judging: Warm orange-red body with a metallic glitter that flashes in patches as you tilt. Look-alike: goldstone, a copper-flecked glass, sparkles uniformly from every angle, shows bubbles, and comes in blue and green; sunstone never does.
sunstone.treatments: Untreated at this tier. Tag: "Natural sunstone (feldspar), India. Untreated." Goldstone must be sold as "goldstone (glass)" (16 CFR 23.25).
sunstone.care: Earrings and necklaces; cleavage makes it chip. Warm soapy water only; no ultrasonic or steam.
sunstone.uses: Warm autumn and southwestern palettes, men's heishi bracelets, a glittering partner for labradorite. Heishi and flat nuggets stand out.
sunstone.carried: Smooth oval, faceted rondelle, square heishi, flat nugget;. Retail: rondelles per 16 inches ; ovals and nuggets per 16 ; half for 8.
talkingPoints: The sparkle is hematite that grew inside the feldspar; glass cannot do patchy.
Goldstone is the fake; here is the tell.
sunstone.folklore: No birthstone; by tradition a stone of joy and personal power.

amazonite.name: Amazonite
amazonite.definition: Blue-green microcline, a potassium feldspar (KAlSi3O8) colored by trace lead and water. Mohs 6 to 6.5, two cleavage directions. Russian material from the Ilmen Mountains shows white albite stripes in a grid or ribbon pattern, hence "Russian banded". Also Peru, Brazil.
amazonite.judging: Saturated teal-blue with crisp white banding tops the Russian line; Peruvian runs paler turquoise blue. Opaque, so judge polish and facet sharpness. Look-alikes: dyed quartzite or howlite (color pools in cracks, no banding), glass (bubbles).
amazonite.treatments: Untreated. Low-grade amazonite is sometimes dyed, which 16 CFR 23.24 requires disclosing. Tag: "Natural amazonite (microcline feldspar), Russia. Untreated."
amazonite.care: Earrings, necklaces and light bracelets; chips on hard knocks along cleavage. Warm soapy water only; no ultrasonic or steam.
amazonite.uses: Summer and coastal palettes, a cheaper "turquoise look", geometric shapes for minimalist designers. Marquise and pear for earrings.
amazonite.carried: Faceted marquise, rectangle, pyramid, pear, including Russian banded; 18 plus 14 SKUs online. No tag observed; bead-market wholesale roughly. Retail: per 8 inches, per 16.
talkingPoints: White stripes are the Russian signature; plain blue is not Russian.
Turquoise color without the stabilizing and dye conversation.
amazonite.folklore: No birthstone; by tradition a "hope" stone.

rhodolite-garnet.name: Rhodolite garnet
rhodolite-garnet.definition: Pyrope-almandine garnet, the purplish red to raspberry garnet. Magnesium-iron aluminum silicate, Mohs 7-7.5, no cleavage. Sources: Tanzania, Mozambique, Sri Lanka, India (Odisha), Madagascar.
rhodolite-garnet.origins: Tanzania, Mozambique, Sri Lanka, India (Odisha), Madagascar
rhodolite-garnet.judging: Even raspberry with a purple flash in daylight and no brown; brick tones mean almandine sold up as rhodolite. Rondelles should be eye-clean and unchipped at the hole. Look-alikes: pink glass (round bubbles, dead-even color) and rubellite tourmaline (pricier; doubles back facets under a loupe, garnet doesn't).
rhodolite-garnet.treatments: Not treated. Tag line: "Rhodolite garnet, natural, not treated." Don't label brownish almandine as rhodolite (16 CFR 23.26, varietal names).
rhodolite-garnet.care: Daily wear. Warm soapy water, soft brush.
rhodolite-garnet.uses: Mid tier. Bead artists pairing pink-red with gold fill or oxidized silver. Rondelles and pear briolettes move fastest.
rhodolite-garnet.carried: Faceted 3mm rondelles, faceted coins, pear and onion briolettes, smooth ovals, and a few strands of large faceted pears. Tags ; large pears. Assume 35 carats per 16-inch strand of 3mm rondelles: retail half for 8 inches. Ovals and coins, 120-150 carats per 16 inches: retail. Large pears: about wholesale per 8-inch strand.
talkingPoints: It's the purple-red garnet, not the brown one.
Hard enough for a ring; it'll outlast the wire.
rhodolite-garnet.folklore: January birthstone; tradition links garnet to friendship and safe travel (tradition, not fact).

red-mozambique-garnet.name: Red Mozambique garnet
red-mozambique-garnet.definition: Almandine-pyrope garnet, sold as "Mozambique garnet" for its clean red with a faint orange warmth. Iron-magnesium aluminum silicate, Mohs 7-7.5, no cleavage. Mined in Mozambique; Indian and Sri Lankan red garnet gets mixed into parcels.
red-mozambique-garnet.judging: Pure red to slightly orange-red in daylight, not purple (that's rhodolite) and not so dark the center goes black. Large ovals always read dark, so judge them against a window. Red glass shows bubbles and swirls and weighs about a third less at the same size.
red-mozambique-garnet.treatments: Not treated. Tag line: "Mozambique garnet (almandine-pyrope), natural, not treated." Don't sell it as rhodolite (16 CFR 23.26) or call red glass "garnet" (23.25(a)).
red-mozambique-garnet.care: Daily-wear hard. Soap, water, soft brush.
red-mozambique-garnet.uses: Entry to mid tier. The workhorse red for holiday pieces and men's 8mm bracelets. Faceted rondelles sell best.
red-mozambique-garnet.carried: Smooth ovals, faceted rondelles and small pears, all tagged. Assume 35 carats per 16 inches of 3mm rondelles: retail or for 8 inches. Smooth ovals run 150-200 carats per 16 inches: retail.
talkingPoints: The classic garnet red at under a dollar a carat.
Same hardness as rhodolite, half the price.
red-mozambique-garnet.folklore: January birthstone; tradition treats garnet as a traveler's protective stone (tradition, not fact).

hessonite-and-spessartite-garnet.name: Hessonite and spessartite garnet
hessonite-and-spessartite-garnet.definition: Hessonite is the cinnamon to honey variety of grossular (calcium aluminum silicate), from Sri Lanka, India and Tanzania. Spessartite is manganese aluminum silicate, brighter mandarin orange, from Nigeria, Namibia and Mozambique. Both Mohs 6.5-7.5; mixed parcels sell as "shaded."
hessonite-and-spessartite-garnet.judging: Hessonite alone shows a swirled, oily "treacle" look inside under a 10x loupe. Citrine is glassy and clean inside, paler, and a same-size strand weighs about 27 percent less (SG 2.65 against 3.65). Fire opal weighs about half as much, is softer (Mohs 5.5-6.5, a steel point scratches it) and often hazy.
hessonite-and-spessartite-garnet.treatments: Neither is treated. Tag lines: "Hessonite garnet, natural, not treated," "Spessartite garnet, natural, not treated," or "Hessonite and spessartite garnet, shaded, natural, not treated" for mixes (16 CFR 23.26).
hessonite-and-spessartite-garnet.uses: Mid tier. Autumn palettes and Vedic astrology buyers asking for "gomed" (hessonite). Shaded heishi and 3mm rondelles sell best.
hessonite-and-spessartite-garnet.carried: Faceted 3-4mm rondelles, pear briolettes, smooth 8mm rounds, ovals, shaded heishi. Tags. Assume 35-60 carats per 16 inches of rondelles: retail half for 8 inches. Smooth 8mm rounds, about 240 carats per 16 inches: retail.
talkingPoints: Look inside; that swirl is the fingerprint of real hessonite.
Fire opal color at garnet hardness.
hessonite-and-spessartite-garnet.folklore: January birthstone; in Indian tradition hessonite (gomed) is worn for the planet Rahu (tradition, not fact).

peridot.name: Peridot
peridot.definition: Gem olivine (forsterite), a magnesium-iron silicate; iron gives the yellow-green. Mohs 6.5-7, no cleavage but brittle. Bead material is mostly Chinese (Hebei) and Pakistani (Kohistan); Arizona (San Carlos) supplies small sizes.
peridot.judging: Pure to slightly yellowish green with no brown; 3mm peridot is never dark. "Lily pad" disc inclusions and tiny black specks are normal and confirm natural origin. Under a loupe peridot shows strong doubling of the far facets; glass doesn't double and shows bubbles. Check drill holes for chipping.
peridot.treatments: Not treated. Tag line: "Peridot, natural, not treated."
peridot.care: Fine for necklaces and earrings, bracelets with care. Soap and water only; no ultrasonic, steam or acids.
peridot.uses: Mid tier. August birthstone pieces, spring greens with freshwater pearl, olive-and-gold palettes. Faceted rondelles and briolettes sell best.
peridot.carried: Faceted 3mm rondelles, ovals, tubes and cubes, pear briolettes. Tags. Assume 30 carats per 16 inches of 3mm rondelles: retail half for 8 inches. Tubes and ovals, about 120 carats per 16 inches: retail. Briolettes, 8-inch strands of 60-80 carats: retail.
talkingPoints: Peridot comes in one color, so every strand matches.
No treatment exists for it; what you see is out of the ground.
peridot.folklore: August birthstone; tradition holds it wards off nightmares (tradition, not fact).

apatite.name: Apatite
apatite.definition: Calcium phosphate with fluorine, chlorine or hydroxyl. Mohs 5, brittle. Neon blue to teal bead material is from Madagascar.
apatite.judging: Saturated electric blue-green, translucent, not milky. Real apatite varies bead to bead, carries needle inclusions, and chips slightly at the holes. A perfectly uniform, clean, cheap hank is often glass or so-called "hydro quartz," which is man-made; loupe for bubbles and swirl lines. Apatite (SG 3.2) is about 25 percent heavier than glass or quartz at the same size; a quartz point scratches it easily.
apatite.treatments: Mostly untreated; some Madagascar material is heated to even the blue (permanent, undetectable). Tag line: "Apatite, natural. May be heated." Man-made material must be labeled "imitation apatite" or "glass," never "apatite" (16 CFR 23.25(a)).
apatite.care: Earrings and necklaces, not bracelets. Damp cloth only; no ultrasonic, heat or acids.
apatite.uses: Upper-mid tier. Designers wanting Paraiba-tourmaline color without the price. Faceted rondelles and heishi sell best.
apatite.carried: Faceted rondelles, heishi, heart and pear briolettes, smooth 8mm rondelles. Tags. Assume 28 carats per 16 inches of 3mm rondelles: retail half for 8 inches. Smooth 8mm rondelles, about 210 carats per 16 inches: retail.
talkingPoints: The Paraiba color at bead prices.
Every strand varies a little; that's how you know it's stone.
apatite.folklore: No birthstone month; tradition calls it a stone for motivation (tradition, not fact).

iolite.name: Iolite
iolite.definition: Gem cordierite, a magnesium-iron aluminum silicate. Mohs 7-7.5, one direction of cleavage. Most bead material is from India; also Tanzania and Sri Lanka. Nicknamed "water sapphire" for its pale sapphire look.
iolite.judging: Iolite is strongly pleochroic: violet-blue in one direction, pale blue-gray in another, straw yellow in the third. In an oval bead one face looks inky and the side washed out; good cutters drill so the blue faces out, so check most beads read blue from the front. Look-alikes: tanzanite (far pricier, different pleochroic colors) and blue glass (no pleochroism, bubbles).
iolite.treatments: Not treated; no treatment works on iolite. Tag line: "Iolite, natural, not treated." Never print "water sapphire" alone; 16 CFR 23.25(a) bars "sapphire" for a stone that isn't sapphire. Write "iolite (nicknamed water sapphire)."
iolite.care: Daily wear is fine; avoid hard knocks along the cleavage. Soap and water.
iolite.uses: Entry tier. Denim and slate palettes, budget "sapphire look" pieces. Faceted heishi sells best.
iolite.carried: Smooth ovals and faceted heishi at. Assume 150 carats per 16 inches of 8x10mm ovals: retail half for 8 inches. Faceted 4mm heishi, 45 carats: retail.
talkingPoints: Turn it; watch the blue come and go. Glass can't do that.
Sapphire hardness at twenty-two cents a carat.
iolite.folklore: Not a modern birthstone; tradition calls it the Viking compass stone (tradition, not fact).

kyanite.name: Kyanite
kyanite.definition: Aluminum silicate that grows as flat blades. Hardness depends on direction: about 4.5-5 along the blade, 6.5-7 across it, hence its old name disthene, "two strengths," plus perfect cleavage in one direction. Blue is mainly Nepalese and Indian; Brazil and East Africa supply teal.
kyanite.judging: Look for even color and a bright polish on the flat face; Nepal blue is the top color. Teal and green are graded for lack of gray. Box and oval beads are sliced parallel to the blade, showing the soft face; check edges for white flaky spots, early cleavage.
kyanite.treatments: Not treated. Tag line: "Kyanite, natural, not treated."
kyanite.care: Necklaces and earrings. Bracelets wear the soft direction fast, and a knock along the blade can split a bead; holes drilled across the blade hold better. Soap and water.
kyanite.uses: Entry to mid tier. Designers who want sapphire blue at a working price. Faceted rondelles and pears sell best.
kyanite.carried: Faceted rondelles, ovals, box beads, 9-10mm pears, smooth ovals; blue, teal and multi. Tags. Assume 55 carats per 16 inches of 4mm rondelles: retail. Ovals and boxes, 200 carats: retail ; 8-inch pear strands.
talkingPoints: Two hardnesses in one stone; harder across, softer along.
Closest blue to sapphire under a dollar a carat.
kyanite.folklore: No birthstone month; tradition says it never needs cleansing (tradition, not fact).

larimar.name: Larimar
larimar.definition: Trade name for blue pectolite, a sodium calcium silicate hydroxide colored by copper. Mohs 4.5-5. One source: Los Chupaderos near Barahona, Dominican Republic.
larimar.disclosureLine: Larimar (blue pectolite), Dominican Republic, natural, not treated.
larimar.judging: Top grade is sky to deep "volcanic" blue with white cloud pattern and no gray or green; the pattern follows radiating fibers, not flat patches. Look-alikes: dyed quartz or agate (glassy, color too even, no fibers), blue calcite (softer, fizzes with vinegar) and glass (bubbles, swirls). A copper coin won't scratch larimar; a steel pin will.
larimar.treatments: Normally untreated; some low grades are waxed or resin-stabilized. Tag lines: "Larimar (blue pectolite), Dominican Republic, natural, not treated" or "Larimar, stabilized (resin-hardened)" (16 CFR 23.24(c): stabilization changes value).
larimar.care: Necklaces and earrings, careful bracelets. The blue can fade after years of sun; store dark. No ultrasonic or heat.
larimar.uses: Upper-mid tier. Beach designers, wire wrappers, collectors of single-source stones. Nuggets and drops sell best; briolettes for earrings.
larimar.carried: Faceted pear briolettes, smooth nuggets, ovals and drops at 10-15mm, rondelles. Nuggets ; briolettes. Assume 240 carats per 16 inches of nuggets: retail half for 8 inches. 8-inch briolette strands : retail.
talkingPoints: One hill in one country; when it's gone, it's gone.
Look for the cloud pattern; imitations can't fake the fibers.
larimar.folklore: No birthstone month; tradition calls it the Atlantis stone (tradition, not fact).

turquoise.name: Turquoise
turquoise.definition: Hydrated copper aluminum phosphate. Mohs 5-6, porous. Bead material comes from Arizona (Kingman still operates; Sleeping Beauty closed in 2012), China (Hubei), Iran and, since 2013, Kazakhstan's Altyn-Tyube deposit (Golden Hills). Mine names can't be lab-confirmed.
turquoise.judging: A hundred identical bright blue beads means stabilized and probably dyed; natural turquoise varies. Chalky white inside the drill hole means dyed magnesite or howlite, whose gray web veins sit on white; dye pools in cracks and rubs onto an acetone swab.
turquoise.treatments: The ladder, best to worst, with tag lines: natural ("Turquoise, natural, not treated"); stabilized, resin soaked in to harden it, the norm ("Turquoise, stabilized"); dyed ("Turquoise, stabilized and dyed"); reconstituted, powder bonded with resin ("Reconstituted turquoise"); imitation ("Imitation turquoise, dyed magnesite"). 16 CFR 23.24(b) and (c) require disclosing stabilization and dye; calling non-turquoise "turquoise" breaks 23.25(a), calling it "natural" breaks 23.27. Unknown history: "Turquoise, assumed stabilized."
turquoise.care: Natural: necklaces and earrings, damp cloth only, no oils or perfume. Stabilized: fine daily. No ultrasonic.
turquoise.uses: Every tier. Southwest and boho designers. Heishi and 4mm rondelles sell best; Golden Hills nuggets are collector items.
turquoise.carried: Arizona-type sky blue: smooth 3-4mm rondelles, heishi, ovals and nuggets, faceted rondelles,. Golden Hills lavender-blue with brown matrix: rondelles and nuggets, about, usually untreated. Green matrix: nuggets and tubes, no tag recorded. Assume 45 carats per 16 inches of 4mm rondelles or heishi: retail half for 8 inches; 200-carat nugget strands.
talkingPoints: Stabilized isn't a dirty word; it makes a soft stone wearable.
Golden Hills is lavender because it grew that way.
turquoise.folklore: December birthstone; tradition calls it a traveler's protector (tradition, not fact).

lapis-lazuli.name: Lapis lazuli
lapis-lazuli.definition: A rock, not a mineral: mostly lazurite with pyrite flecks and calcite. Mohs 5-6. Best material: Badakhshan, Afghanistan; Chile supplies most calcite-rich "denim" grade.
lapis-lazuli.judging: Grades: top is deep royal blue with gold pyrite and no visible white; middle has more pyrite and calcite spots; denim is pale with much calcite. Low-end lapis is often dyed to hide calcite; an acetone swab picks up blue. Sodalite, the usual substitute, is purplish with white veins and no pyrite; dyed jasper ("Swiss lapis") and howlite are imitations.
lapis-lazuli.treatments: Wax polish is normal and needs no tag; dye does. Tag lines: "Lapis lazuli, natural, not dyed" or "Lapis lazuli, dyed" (16 CFR 23.24(a) and (c): dye can wear off and changes value); "Swiss lapis" breaks 23.25(a).
lapis-lazuli.care: Pendants and earrings daily, bracelets with care. Mild soap, soft brush; no ultrasonic or solvents.
lapis-lazuli.uses: Entry to mid tier. Navy-and-gold palettes, men's bracelets. Faceted 5mm rondelles and 8mm rounds sell best.
lapis-lazuli.carried: Faceted 5mm rondelles, daggers, cubes, tubes, smooth rounds, graduated rondelles, denim-grade ovals. Tags. Assume 70 carats per 16 inches of 5mm rondelles: retail half for 8 inches.
talkingPoints: The gold flecks are pyrite; that's how you know it's lapis.
Deep blue with almost no white is the Afghan grade.
lapis-lazuli.folklore: Older lists make it a December birthstone; tradition ties it to truth (tradition, not fact).

chrysocolla-and-shattuckite.name: Chrysocolla and shattuckite
chrysocolla-and-shattuckite.definition: Two blue-green copper silicates that grow together. Chrysocolla is Mohs 2.5-3.5 alone but up to 7 locked in chalcedony or quartz, the bead-grade form, from Peru, DR Congo and Arizona. Shattuckite (Mohs about 3.5) was named for Bisbee's Shattuck mine; most now comes from the Kaokoveld, Namibia.
chrysocolla-and-shattuckite.disclosureLine: Chrysocolla in quartz, natural, not treated,.
chrysocolla-and-shattuckite.judging: Chrysocolla is robin's-egg to sky blue-green with a waxy to glassy finish; shattuckite is deeper, near-royal blue in fibrous patches, often with black or green. The usual confusion is azurite-malachite, a carbonate: azurite is deep navy, malachite green in concentric bands. Vinegar on a hidden spot fizzes on azurite-malachite, not on the silicates.
chrysocolla-and-shattuckite.treatments: Beads are often resin-stabilized because the mineral is soft; some are dyed. Tag lines: "Chrysocolla in quartz, natural, not treated," "Chrysocolla, stabilized," or "Chrysocolla, stabilized and dyed" (16 CFR 23.24(b) and (c)). Don't call it "Eilat stone" unless it's from Israel (23.26).
chrysocolla-and-shattuckite.care: Necklaces and earrings. Damp cloth; no ultrasonic, acids or perfume.
chrysocolla-and-shattuckite.uses: Mid tier. Southwest palettes as a turquoise alternative. Nuggets and ovals sell best.
chrysocolla-and-shattuckite.carried: Smooth ovals, nuggets and heishi. No tag recorded on 2026-09-04; assume about wholesale and 180 carats per 16 inches of ovals: retail. Heishi, 45 carats:.
talkingPoints: Copper-stained quartz that looks like turquoise and wears harder.
Vinegar test: this won't fizz; azurite will.
chrysocolla-and-shattuckite.folklore: No birthstone month; tradition calls it a stone of communication (tradition, not fact).

fluorite.name: Fluorite
fluorite.definition: Calcium fluoride. Mohs 4, perfect cleavage in four directions. Banded "rainbow" bead material comes almost entirely from China.
fluorite.disclosureLine: Fluorite, natural, not treated. Soft stone, handle with care.
fluorite.judging: Saturated bands with sharp color changes and good transparency; gray or mostly colorless beads are the low end. Faceted tubes should have crisp facet junctions; a rushed polish rounds them. Check drill holes for flat or stepped chips, early cleavage.
fluorite.treatments: Not treated, apart from occasional wax. Tag line: "Fluorite, natural, not treated. Soft stone, handle with care." 16 CFR 23.24 doesn't require it for an untreated stone; print it anyway.
fluorite.care: Mohs 4 in plain terms: a steel pin, a key or house dust (quartz, Mohs 7) will scratch it, and a knock on a table edge can split a bead along a cleavage plane. Earrings and necklaces only; never bracelets or rings. Cool soapy water; no ultrasonic, heat or acids.
fluorite.uses: Entry tier. Candy palettes, crystal-shop buyers, gift lines. Rondelles and heishi sell best.
fluorite.carried: Smooth rondelles, faceted tubes and heishi in banded multicolor at. Assume 120 carats per 16 inches of 6-8mm rondelles: retail half for 8 inches.
talkingPoints: Every bead is a slice through a different set of color bands.
Treat it like glass and it'll last.
fluorite.folklore: No birthstone month; tradition calls it the "genius stone" for focus (tradition, not fact).

seraphinite.name: Seraphinite
seraphinite.definition: Trade name for clinochlore, a chlorite-group magnesium-iron aluminum silicate, in a form with silvery mica-like feathers on dark green. Mohs 2-2.5, among the softest beads sold. One source: the Korshunovskoye iron mine in Irkutsk Oblast, Eastern Siberia.
seraphinite.disclosureLine: Seraphinite (clinochlore), Russia, natural, not treated. Very soft stone.
seraphinite.judging: A strong silver "angel wing" shimmer that moves as you tilt the strand, on deep green rather than gray-green. Check for flaking at drill holes and edges; chlorite is layered and peels. Nothing else has the feather pattern.
seraphinite.treatments: Not treated. Tag line: "Seraphinite (clinochlore), Russia, natural, not treated. Very soft stone." 16 CFR 23.24 doesn't require it for an untreated stone; print it anyway.
seraphinite.care: A fingernail can mark it. Earrings and short necklaces worn occasionally; never bracelets. Dry or barely damp cloth; no soaking or chemicals.
seraphinite.uses: Entry to mid tier. Crystal-shop and metaphysical buyers, earring makers. 4mm rondelles and heishi are the whole market; it's too soft for large beads.
seraphinite.carried: Smooth 4mm rondelles and heishi. No tag recorded on 2026-09-04; assume about wholesale. Assume 40 carats per 16 inches: retail half for 8 inches.
talkingPoints: Tilt it; those silver feathers are why it's named for the seraphim.
One mine in Siberia, nowhere else.
seraphinite.folklore: No birthstone month; tradition calls it an angel stone (tradition, not fact).

charoite.name: Charoite
charoite.definition: A rare potassium calcium sodium silicate with a fibrous, swirling purple structure. Mohs 5-6. One source: the Murun massif on the Chara River, Sakha Republic (Yakutia), Russia; described in 1978. It's a rock: black aegirine, orange tinaksite and white feldspar sit in the purple.
charoite.judging: Strong lilac to violet with a chatoyant swirl, like silk. Black and orange specks are normal and prove it isn't dyed; too much black or white lowers the grade. Look-alikes: dyed resin composites and glass (no fibers, uniform color, bubbles) and sugilite (grape purple, waxy, no swirl, far pricier).
charoite.treatments: Usually untreated; some material is resin-stabilized or waxed. Tag lines: "Charoite, Russia, natural, not treated" or "Charoite, stabilized" (16 CFR 23.24(c)). Never sell purple resin as charoite (23.25(a)).
charoite.care: Necklaces and earrings daily; bracelets with care. Soap and water; no ultrasonic or heat.
charoite.uses: Upper tier. Collectors of single-source stones, purple-palette designers, wire wrappers. Large ovals sell; small beads lose the swirl.
charoite.carried: One strand of smooth 12-16mm ovals. No tag recorded on 2026-09-04; assume about wholesale and 165 carats per 16 inches: retail.
talkingPoints: One valley in Siberia, and the Russians control the supply.
Turn it and watch the silk move.
charoite.folklore: No birthstone month; tradition calls it a stone of transformation (tradition, not fact).

rhodochrosite.name: Rhodochrosite
rhodochrosite.definition: Manganese carbonate. Mohs 3.5-4, perfect cleavage in three directions. Banded pink-and-cream bead material comes from the Capillitas mine, Catamarca, Argentina, where it formed as stalactites in old copper-silver workings, hence "Inca Rose."
rhodochrosite.disclosureLine: Rhodochrosite, Argentina, natural, not treated. Soft stone.
rhodochrosite.judging: Strong rose to raspberry bands alternating with cream or white, sharp and concentric, with translucency at the edges. Pale, mostly cream beads are the low grade. Look-alikes: rhodonite (harder, opaque, black veins, no bands), dyed agate (bands too regular, color in cracks), pink calcite (no banding). A drop of vinegar at the drill hole fizzes on rhodochrosite and calcite, not agate or rhodonite; rinse at once.
rhodochrosite.treatments: Not usually treated; some lower material is waxed or resin-stabilized. Tag lines: "Rhodochrosite, Argentina, natural, not treated. Soft stone" or "Rhodochrosite, stabilized" (16 CFR 23.24(c)).
rhodochrosite.care: Necklaces and earrings only. Perfume, sweat and any acid etch it. Damp cloth and dry; no soaking, ultrasonic or heat.
rhodochrosite.uses: Mid tier. Pink palettes, single-focal necklaces. Large ovals show the bands; small rondelles don't.
rhodochrosite.carried: Smooth banded ovals at 15-20mm,. Assume 290 carats per 16 inches: retail or for 8 inches.
talkingPoints: It grew as a stalactite in an old silver mine; the bands are growth rings.
Argentina's national stone.
rhodochrosite.folklore: No birthstone month; tradition calls it a stone of compassion (tradition, not fact).

pink-opal.name: Pink opal
pink-opal.definition: Common opal (opal-CT with the clay mineral palygorskite), pink from organic compounds, no play-of-color. Mohs 5.5 to 6.5. Rough from Peru, mainly the Acari area of Arequipa.
pink-opal.disclosureLine: Natural Peruvian pink opal (common opal). Untreated.
pink-opal.judging: Even warm pink without gray; cream mottling is normal and cheaper; never glassy. Look-alikes: rhodonite (harder, black veins), dyed chalcedony or magnesite (color pooled in drill holes at 10x; an acetone swab lifts it).
pink-opal.treatments: Normally none; the tray showed no dye. Tag: "Natural Peruvian pink opal (common opal). Untreated." If a lot fails the swab: "Dyed pink opal" (16 CFR 23.24). Never imply play-of-color (23.1).
pink-opal.care: Earrings and necklaces; bracelets scuff. Porous: no ultrasonic, perfume, soaking or heat.
pink-opal.uses: Soft-palette designers: bridal, spring, baby pieces, gold-fill bracelets. Mid tier. Rounds, heishi and tubes sell best.
pink-opal.carried: Smooth round 8 to 10mm, rondelle, oval 12 to 18mm, heishi, faceted tube, cube; tags. At 65 ct per 8 inches of 8mm rounds, retail per 8 inch, per 16; the + lots only pay at the top.
talkingPoints: softer than rose quartz, keep it off rings.
pink-opal.folklore: Tradition calls it a stone of emotional calm; tradition, not fact.

peruvian-blue-opal-and-multi-peruvian-op.name: Peruvian blue opal and multi Peruvian opal
peruvian-blue-opal-and-multi-peruvian-op.definition: Common opal from the same copper-country deposits as pink opal (Acari, Arequipa); blue-green credited to copper, dendrites to manganese oxide. Mohs 5.5 to 6.5. "Multi Peruvian opal" is mixed pink, blue, green and tan common opal.
peruvian-blue-opal-and-multi-peruvian-op.disclosureLine: Natural Peruvian blue opal with matrix. Untreated.
peruvian-blue-opal-and-multi-peruvian-op.judging: Blue: clean sky to teal with sharp dendrites is the top; muddy gray-green with heavy matrix the bottom. Multi should look soft and slightly uneven; hot orange or candy pink beads, or color pooled in drill holes, mean dyed chalcedony.
peruvian-blue-opal-and-multi-peruvian-op.treatments: Blue: none seen. Tag: "Natural Peruvian blue opal with matrix. Untreated." Multi: swab-test orange and pink beads. Clean: "Multi Peruvian opal, natural color." Failed: "Multi opal strand; orange and pink beads are dyed chalcedony" (23.24, 23.1). Never "may be dyed."
peruvian-blue-opal-and-multi-peruvian-op.care: As pink opal: no ultrasonic, chemicals, heat or soaking. Dyed sections fade in sun.
peruvian-blue-opal-and-multi-peruvian-op.uses: Blue ovals: focal pendants, upper-mid tier. Multi rondelles: beachy, boho work, entry tier.
peruvian-blue-opal-and-multi-peruvian-op.carried: Blue smooth oval 10x14 with dendritic matrix, ; multi rondelles 5 to 7mm,. At 110 ct per 8 inches of ovals and 60 ct of rondelles, blue ovals retail per 8 inch ; multi.
talkingPoints: we test every pastel lot for dye.
peruvian-blue-opal-and-multi-peruvian-op.folklore: Tradition ties blue opal to calm speech; tradition, not fact.

dendrite-opal.name: Dendrite opal
dendrite-opal.definition: White common opal with black tree-like manganese-oxide inclusions; hydrated silica, Mohs 5.5 to 6; rough from Kazakhstan, Turkey, Mexico, Madagascar. "Dendrite opal" is the Indian trade name; "dendritic agate" is the same picture in harder chalcedony (6.5 to 7); "merlinite" is a New Mexico crystal-shop name applied to either.
dendrite-opal.disclosureLine: Natural dendritic opal (common opal with manganese dendrites). Untreated. Sold as dendrite opal or merlinite.
dendrite-opal.judging: Crisp black ferns on a clean white ground, one full dendrite per dagger. A steel point scratches opal at the drill-hole edge and skates on agate. Look-alike: printed glass (bubbles; surface pattern only).
dendrite-opal.treatments: None normal. Tag: "Natural dendritic opal (common opal with manganese dendrites). Untreated. Sold as dendrite opal or merlinite." If a lot is chalcedony: "Natural dendritic agate." Wrong species is a 23.26 varietal-name problem.
dendrite-opal.care: Softer than quartz; no rings, ultrasonic or heat. Water, soft cloth.
dendrite-opal.uses: Minimalist and neutral-palette designers, wedding work. Entry to mid tier. Daggers and kites sell best.
