dendrite-opal.carried: Smooth round 12mm, heishi 5mm, faceted dagger 30mm; 18 online SKUs at. Tag not read. At 170 ct per 8 inches of 12mm rounds, retail per 8 inch, per 16.
talkingPoints: it's opal, treat it like opal, not quartz.
dendrite-opal.folklore: Tradition links dendritic stones to growth; tradition, not fact.

chrysoprase.name: Chrysoprase
chrysoprase.definition: Chalcedony colored apple green by nickel; Mohs 6.5 to 7. Rough from Queensland and Western Australia, Tanzania, Indonesia. "Lemon chrysoprase" is not chrysoprase: it is nickel-bearing magnesite (magnesium carbonate) from Western Australia, Mohs about 3.5 to 4.5.
chrysoprase.disclosureLine: Natural chrysoprase (nickel chalcedony), Australia or Tanzania. Untreated.
chrysoprase.judging: Even apple green with a translucent glow is the top; grayish and opaque is commercial; brown spots lower it. Look-alikes: dyed green chalcedony (too even, often bluish), aventurine (mica glitter). Lemon magnesite is opaque, light, and a steel point scratches it.
chrysoprase.treatments: Chrysoprase: none. Tag: "Natural chrysoprase (nickel chalcedony), Australia or Tanzania. Untreated." Lemon: "Citron magnesite, sold in the trade as lemon chrysoprase. Not chrysoprase. Natural color." Calling magnesite chrysoprase breaks 23.26 (varietal name) and 23.1.
chrysoprase.care: Fades with prolonged heat or sun; store dark; no ultrasonic. Magnesite is soft: earrings and necklaces only.
chrysoprase.uses: Fine-jewelry designers and collectors; the high-ticket strand. Rounds and rondelles sell.
chrysoprase.carried: Smooth round 8mm, rondelle 6 to 9mm, oval 10 to 18mm; tags. At 85 ct per 8 inches of 8mm rounds, cost is ; retail per 8 inch, per 16. The most valuable stone in this tier.
talkingPoints: the lemon one is magnesite, priced as magnesite.
chrysoprase.folklore: Tradition names chrysoprase the stone of optimism; tradition, not fact.

blue-and-lavender-chalcedony.name: Blue and lavender chalcedony
blue-and-lavender-chalcedony.definition: Chalcedony whose blue comes from light scattering off microscopic voids, not pigment, so natural material looks milky, grayish or lilac. Mohs 6.5 to 7. Sources: Namibia, Turkey, Montana, Oregon. "Lavender moon quartz" is a trade name hung on lavender chalcedony, sometimes dyed or lab-made.
blue-and-lavender-chalcedony.disclosureLine: Natural blue chalcedony, Namibia or Turkey. Untreated.
blue-and-lavender-chalcedony.judging: Natural: soft cloudy blue with a faint inner glow. Dyed: vivid uniform periwinkle on every strand. Loupe drill holes for pooled color; acetone-swab one bead; pink through a Chelsea filter means dye. His uniform "lavender moon quartz" pears are a flag.
blue-and-lavender-chalcedony.treatments: Natural blue chalcedony is untreated. Tag: "Natural blue chalcedony, Namibia or Turkey. Untreated." If tested dyed: "Dyed chalcedony (lavender). Color can fade with sun, bleach or solvents" (23.24: permanence uncertain, value affected).
blue-and-lavender-chalcedony.care: Hard enough for bracelets. Keep dyed beads out of sun, bleach and pools.
blue-and-lavender-chalcedony.uses: Statement ovals for pendants; faceted pears for earrings. Upper-mid tier if natural. Rondelles and pears sell fastest.
blue-and-lavender-chalcedony.carried: Smooth oval 10x14, rondelle, nugget, faceted pear; tag. At 135 ct per 8 inches of ovals, cost is about so retail must be per 8 inch, which only holds if natural; dyed chalcedony retails at per 16 inch.
talkingPoints: neon lavender and cheap means dyed; we tag it.
blue-and-lavender-chalcedony.folklore: Tradition calls it the speaker's stone; tradition, not fact.

carnelian.name: Carnelian
carnelian.definition: Chalcedony colored orange to red by iron oxide; Mohs 6.5 to 7. Rough and cutting: India (Gujarat has cut carnelian for millennia), Brazil, Uruguay, Madagascar.
carnelian.disclosureLine: Carnelian (chalcedony), heat-treated to deepen color, standard for this stone.
carnelian.judging: Translucent warm orange-red with soft cloudy zoning is the natural look. Held to the light, parallel stripes mean banded agate, heated or dyed, sold as carnelian for less; dead-even brick red across a strand means iron-dyed agate. Look-alike: orange glass (bubbles).
carnelian.treatments: Almost all commercial carnelian is heated to deepen the red; much is agate dyed with iron salts. Heat is permanent and needs no care, so 23.24 does not strictly demand it, but say it: "Carnelian (chalcedony), heat-treated to deepen color, standard for this stone." Dyed: "Dyed agate, carnelian color" (23.24, 23.26).
carnelian.care: Tough. Warm soapy water, soft brush. Avoid prolonged heat.
carnelian.uses: Fall palettes, boho and southwestern work, men's bracelets, mala makers. Entry tier. Smooth pears and 8mm rounds sell.
carnelian.carried: Smooth pear 10x14 with natural zoning, faceted rondelle and nugget; two online SKUs. Tag not read. At 100 ct per 8 inches of pears, retail per 8 inch, per 16.
talkingPoints: heated, like nearly all carnelian; most sellers don't tell you.
carnelian.folklore: Tradition makes carnelian a stone of courage; tradition, not fact.

black-onyx-and-black-spinel.name: Black onyx and black spinel
black-onyx-and-black-spinel.definition: Two stones. Black onyx is chalcedony (Mohs 6.5 to 7), nearly all of it gray agate dyed black by the sugar-and-sulfuric-acid method used since 19th-century Idar-Oberstein; natural solid-black chalcedony is rare. Black spinel is natural magnesium aluminum oxide, Mohs 8, from Thailand, Myanmar and Sri Lanka.
black-onyx-and-black-spinel.disclosureLine: Black onyx: chalcedony dyed black (sugar-acid treatment). Permanent; standard for all black onyx.
black-onyx-and-black-spinel.judging: Onyx: dense even black, no gray bleed at facet edges. Spinel: glassier (higher refractive index) and heavy for its size. Dyed onyx often shows a lighter core or white banding at the drill hole; spinel is black through and scratches onyx.
black-onyx-and-black-spinel.treatments: Onyx: "Black onyx: chalcedony dyed black (sugar-acid treatment). Permanent; standard for all black onyx." Accepted, but it affects value, so 23.24(c) applies. Spinel: "Natural black spinel, Thailand. Untreated."
black-onyx-and-black-spinel.care: Both take daily wear and ultrasonic; keep onyx out of bleach.
black-onyx-and-black-spinel.uses: Onyx: men's and minimalist lines. Spinel: natural black at fine-jewelry hardness. Daggers, marquise and rondelles sell best.
black-onyx-and-black-spinel.carried: Onyx faceted marquise, dagger, pear, rondelle, tube, kite, bar, 15 to 45mm; 14 onyx SKUs online, 6 spinel. At 200 ct per 8 inches of 25mm marquise, onyx retails per 8 inch, per 16; spinel.
talkingPoints: onyx is dyed, all of it; for natural black, buy spinel.
black-onyx-and-black-spinel.folklore: Tradition calls both protective grounding stones; tradition, not fact.

green-onyx-and-green-aventurine.name: Green onyx and green aventurine
green-onyx-and-green-aventurine.definition: In the bead trade "green onyx" is agate or chalcedony (Mohs 6.5 to 7) dyed green (carvers' "green onyx" is banded calcite). Green aventurine is natural Indian quartzite (Mohs 6.5 to 7) full of fuchsite, a chromium mica that gives the green and a faint glitter (aventurescence).
green-onyx-and-green-aventurine.disclosureLine: Green onyx: chalcedony (agate) dyed green. Avoid bleach and strong sun.
green-onyx-and-green-aventurine.judging: Green onyx: uniform bottle green, translucent, no color pooled in drill holes. Aventurine: opaque medium green with mica flecks at 10x; that glitter is the ID, no dyed chalcedony has it. Look-alike: glass (bubbles).
green-onyx-and-green-aventurine.treatments: Green onyx: "Green onyx: chalcedony (agate) dyed green. Avoid bleach and strong sun." Required under 23.24; the tag must say chalcedony because the name alone is a 23.26 problem. Aventurine: "Natural green aventurine (quartzite with fuchsite), India. Untreated."
green-onyx-and-green-aventurine.care: Both fine for bracelets. Dyed onyx: no ultrasonic or bleach.
green-onyx-and-green-aventurine.uses: Onyx: emerald-color statement shapes cheap. Aventurine: budget "lucky green" bracelets, men's malas. Entry tier. Marquise and kites move.
green-onyx-and-green-aventurine.carried: Green onyx faceted pear, marquise, rondelle, kite, bar; 13 SKUs online. Aventurine faceted pear and marquise, not yet online. At 200 ct per 8 inches of 25mm marquise, onyx retails per 8 inch, per 16; aventurine.
talkingPoints: green onyx is dyed chalcedony; natural green is aventurine or chrysoprase.
green-onyx-and-green-aventurine.folklore: Tradition calls aventurine the gambler's luck stone; tradition, not fact.

bumble-bee-jasper.name: Bumble bee jasper
bumble-bee-jasper.definition: Not a jasper. A soft fumarole rock from West Java, Indonesia (Mount Ciremai area; sold as Papandayan): fibrous calcite with native sulfur (yellow), the arsenic sulfides realgar and orpiment (orange), pyrite and manganese oxides (black). Mohs 3 to 5.
bumble-bee-jasper.disclosureLine: Bumble bee jasper (trade name): calcite rock with sulfur and arsenic sulfide minerals, Indonesia. Not a jasper. Resin-stabilized. Soft; keep dry.
bumble-bee-jasper.judging: Bright lemon and orange bands with clean black divisions; more yellow, better. Facets this soft are never razor sharp; look for even polish and bands running through the bead. Look-alike: dyed calcite (dead uniform).
bumble-bee-jasper.treatments: Nearly all beads are epoxy-stabilized to seal the porous, arsenic-bearing surface; confirm with the cutter. Tag: "Bumble bee jasper (trade name): calcite rock with sulfur and arsenic sulfide minerals, Indonesia. Not a jasper. Resin-stabilized. Soft; keep dry." Required under 23.24(b) (special care) and 23.26 (wrong name).
bumble-bee-jasper.care: Earrings and pendants only. No soaking, acids or ultrasonic. Never grind or drill a bead; the dust carries arsenic. Sealed beads are safe to wear.
bumble-bee-jasper.uses: Bold-color designers, statement earrings, collectors. Upper-mid tier by strand. Marquise and large pears sell.
bumble-bee-jasper.carried: Faceted pear 10 to 40mm, marquise 25 to 30mm, hearts, arrowheads, triangles; 8 SKUs online. Tag not read. At 180 ct per 8 inches of 25mm marquise, retail per 8 inch, per 16. Sells by the strand.
talkingPoints: it's soft calcite, so it's an earring stone.
bumble-bee-jasper.folklore: Tradition treats it as a confidence stone; tradition, not fact.

k2-granite.name: K2 granite
k2-granite.definition: Not a jasper. White granite (quartz, plagioclase, muscovite, biotite) with round orbs of blue azurite, from the foot of K2 in the Karakoram, Skardu district, Pakistan. Granite is Mohs 6 to 7, azurite 3.5 to 4, but the azurite is a stain along grain boundaries, so the orbs polish like the granite.
k2-granite.disclosureLine: K2 granite (sold as K2 jasper): natural white granite with azurite orbs, Skardu, Pakistan. Untreated. Not a jasper.
k2-granite.judging: Clean white ground with several saturated blue orbs per bead is the top; gray speckled ground with one faint dot the bottom (price the gray lot lower). Orbs should be soft-edged, fading into granite that glitters with mica. Look-alike: dyed howlite with painted spots (color in cracks).
k2-granite.treatments: None; the azurite is natural, confirmed by X-ray diffraction. Tag: "K2 granite (sold as K2 jasper): natural white granite with azurite orbs, Skardu, Pakistan. Untreated. Not a jasper." The parenthetical satisfies 23.26.
k2-granite.care: Necklaces and earrings; feldspar scratches in bracelets. Soapy water; no acids, which attack azurite.
k2-granite.uses: Men's and unisex lines, "modern rustic" designers. Mid tier. Marquise, bars and kites sell.
k2-granite.carried: Faceted marquise 25 to 30mm, rectangle 15 to 25mm, pyramid, kite, slices; 12 SKUs online at. Tag not read. At 200 ct per 8 inches of 25mm marquise, retail per 8 inch, per 16.
talkingPoints: granite, not jasper, and the tag says so.
k2-granite.folklore: Tradition calls K2 a stone of balance; tradition, not fact.

pyrite.name: Pyrite
pyrite.definition: Iron sulfide, FeS2, "fool's gold." Metallic brass-yellow, Mohs 6 to 6.5 but brittle, and heavy (specific gravity about 5, twice chalcedony). It oxidizes slowly in humid air into iron sulfates and traces of sulfuric acid ("pyrite decay"). Rough is mostly Peruvian (Huanzala district) and Chinese.
pyrite.disclosureLine: Natural pyrite (iron sulfide), Peru. Untreated. Tarnishes with moisture; keep dry.
pyrite.judging: Even brass color, mirror-bright facets, no dull brown patches (early tarnish), crisp edges, no cracks radiating from drill holes. Look-alikes: hematite (gray-black), gold-tone coated glass (too light). Real pyrite leaves a greenish-black streak on unglazed tile.
pyrite.treatments: None normal; some cutters lacquer beads to slow tarnish, so ask. Tag: "Natural pyrite (iron sulfide), Peru. Untreated. Tarnishes with moisture; keep dry." If lacquered, add "lacquer-coated" (23.24(b)).
pyrite.care: Dry box with silica gel; wipe after wear; never shower, swim or sleep in it. Not for rings.
pyrite.uses: Men's bracelets, mixed-metal and industrial styles. Entry to mid tier. Bars, daggers and heishi sell best.
pyrite.carried: Faceted pear, marquise, dagger, rectangle, bar 10 to 40mm, heishi 5mm; 8 SKUs online. Tags not read. At 400 ct per 8 inches of 25mm marquise, retail per 8 inch, per 16. Price by the strand; per-carat looks misleadingly cheap.
talkingPoints: gold
fool's gold hates humidity; keep it dry.
pyrite.folklore: Tradition calls pyrite a money stone; tradition, not fact.

ruby-zoisite.name: Ruby zoisite
ruby-zoisite.definition: A metamorphic rock from the Mundarara mine near Longido, Tanzania: green zoisite with opaque red to pink ruby (corundum) and black hornblende. Hardness is mixed, zoisite Mohs 6 to 7, ruby 9, so the ruby stands proud on polished beads.
ruby-zoisite.disclosureLine: Natural ruby in zoisite (anyolite), Longido, Tanzania. Untreated.
ruby-zoisite.judging: Buyers want all three colors on every bead: strong green, clear red, some black; mostly green with pink specks is commercial. Facets undercut where soft zoisite meets hard corundum; feel for grooves. Look-alike: ruby-in-fuchsite (softer, sparkly mica).
ruby-zoisite.treatments: None. Tag: "Natural ruby in zoisite (anyolite), Longido, Tanzania. Untreated." Don't quote a ruby carat weight or imply gem ruby; the corundum is opaque (23.1). The online "Ruby Glass Filled" heart filed under Ruby Zoisite belongs under treated ruby.
ruby-zoisite.care: Sturdy for necklaces and earrings; bracelets with care. Soapy water; no ultrasonic on faceted pieces.
ruby-zoisite.uses: Holiday designers, watermelon-palette fans, men's lines wanting color. Mid tier. Marquise and daggers move fastest.
ruby-zoisite.carried: Faceted pear 10 to 40mm, marquise 25mm, dagger 25 to 30mm; 11 online SKUs. One bundle tagged. At 30 grams per 8 inches of 25mm marquise, cost is about ; retail per 8 inch, per 16.
talkingPoints: the ruby is opaque, not gem grade, which is why a strand costs $45 not $4,500.
ruby-zoisite.folklore: Tradition pairs it with vitality; tradition, not fact.

freshwater-cultured-pearl.name: Freshwater cultured pearl
freshwater-cultured-pearl.definition: Nacre (mostly aragonite with conchiolin) grown by freshwater mussels on Chinese farms; China is the only commercial producer. Mohs 2.5 to 4.5. Rounds are tissue-nucleated solid nacre; "fireball" pearls are bead-nucleated baroques with a round body and flame-shaped tail.
freshwater-cultured-pearl.disclosureLine: Freshwater cultured pearl, China. White, bleached (standard).
freshwater-cultured-pearl.judging: Luster is everything: sharp reflections mean thick nacre, fuzzy means thin. Fireballs want a blemish-light body and metallic tail; rounds want matched size and few pits. Imitations peel at the drill hole; dye pools there.
freshwater-cultured-pearl.treatments: Whites are routinely bleached; pink, lavender and peach can be natural; other colors are dyed or irradiated. Tag: "Freshwater cultured pearl, China. White, bleached (standard)." Dyed: "Freshwater cultured pearl, dyed." "Cultured" must sit beside "pearl" at equal size (16 CFR 23.20(b)); treatments fall under 23.23; never "natural pearl" (23.21(e)).
freshwater-cultured-pearl.care: Last on, first off. No perfume, acids or ultrasonic. Damp cloth.
freshwater-cultured-pearl.uses: Bridal and classic designers, single-fireball pendants, layering necklaces. Mid tier.
freshwater-cultured-pearl.carried: Baroque fireball 15 to 25mm and round 8 to 10mm, white with pink or mauve overtone; printed tags read as retail stickers. Assuming 16-inch strands, fireballs retail by luster and tail; rounds. Resale stock, not Jaipur.
talkingPoints: shell pearl.
cultured freshwater, bleached white like every white pearl.
freshwater-cultured-pearl.folklore: Tradition calls pearls tears of the moon; tradition, not fact.

glass-hydro-quartz-coated-and-dyed-mater.name: Glass, hydro quartz, coated and dyed material
glass-hydro-quartz-coated-and-dyed-mater.definition: Four lots that are not what their color says. (1) "Hydro quartz" faceted hearts and pears 8 to 10mm in emerald, citrine, Swiss-blue, peridot and pink colors, $0.25 per carat in 1,990 ct lots. True hydrothermal quartz is laboratory-grown quartz (Mohs 7, quartz chemistry); Jaipur sellers also use the name for colored glass, and at this price the photo notes call these glass. (2) "Mystic" rainbow-coated quartz: a thin metallic surface film, not permanent. (3) Dyed chalcedony rondelle sets. (4) Dyed Ethiopian opal rondelles: hydrophane Welo opal soaks up dye; GIA found it pooled in pits and leaching out in peroxide.
glass-hydro-quartz-coated-and-dyed-mater.judging: Identify, don't grade. Glass shows round bubbles and swirl lines at 10x and a quartz point scratches it; lab quartz has neither. Eye-clean, matched, under $0.50 per carat in emerald or Paraiba color is not the stone it resembles.
glass-hydro-quartz-coated-and-dyed-mater.treatments: 23.25(a), (b): a gemstone name may not describe anything that is not that mined stone unless "laboratory-grown," "imitation" or "simulated" immediately precedes it with equal conspicuousness. 23.25(c): "lab-created emerald" is barred for green quartz. 23.27: "natural," "genuine" or "real" may never describe artificial products. 23.24: non-permanent or value-affecting coatings and dyes must be disclosed. 23.1 bars misrepresenting substance or treatment generally. Tags. Glass: "Imitation emerald color, glass." Confirmed lab quartz: "Laboratory-grown quartz, green." Never "hydro emerald" or "emerald quartz." Coated: "Coated quartz, rainbow film. Not permanent; avoid abrasives." Dyed chalcedony: "Dyed chalcedony." Dyed opal: "Dyed Ethiopian opal (hydrophane). Dye may fade or leach; keep dry."
glass-hydro-quartz-coated-and-dyed-mater.care: Glass and lab quartz: ordinary. Coated: soft cloth only. Dyed opal: no water.
glass-hydro-quartz-coated-and-dyed-mater.uses: Costume and fast-fashion makers who want color for nothing. Bottom tier.
glass-hydro-quartz-coated-and-dyed-mater.carried: About 25 hydro strands, 12 to 14 coated, several dyed chalcedony sets, one tray of dyed opal. An 8-inch hydro strand cost ; retail as glass.
talkingPoints: glass and treated
this is glass, priced like glass, and it photographs like emerald.
glass-hydro-quartz-coated-and-dyed-mater.folklore: Don't sell hydro quartz, coated quartz or dyed opal under the Tandon Gems name; the Instagram bio says "100% natural," and $15 glass strands put that claim and every $500 chrysoprase strand at risk. Clear the lots at one show in a labeled bin; don't list or restock. Dyed chalcedony sets can stay if every tag says "dyed chalcedony."

multi-gemstone-heishi-and-designer-mix-s.name: Multi-gemstone heishi and designer mix strands
multi-gemstone-heishi-and-designer-mix-s.definition: Strands assembled in Jaipur from cutting-room remainders: 4 to 5mm heishi mixing carnelian, chalcedony, chrysoprase, amethyst, moonstone and opal, and large tyre mixes of lapis, amazonite, pink opal and sunstone. Only as tough as the softest bead (opal, Mohs 5.5 to 6).
multi-gemstone-heishi-and-designer-mix-s.disclosureLine: Designer mix: lapis lazuli, amazonite, pink opal, sunstone (natural) with dyed chalcedony accents.
multi-gemstone-heishi-and-designer-mix-s.judging: A good mix has a repeating color plan, even sizing, and no filler. His hot pink and turquoise heishi look dyed. Identify by species, not color; dyed chalcedony is glassy with color in the drill hole.
multi-gemstone-heishi-and-designer-mix-s.treatments: Name every component and flag any dyed one (23.1, 23.24, 23.26). Large mix: "Designer mix: lapis lazuli, amazonite, pink opal, sunstone (natural) with dyed chalcedony accents." Small heishi: "Multi-gemstone heishi: carnelian (heated), chalcedony (some dyed), amethyst, moonstone, chrysoprase, opal."
multi-gemstone-heishi-and-designer-mix-s.care: Treat as opal: no ultrasonic, chemicals or soaking.
multi-gemstone-heishi-and-designer-mix-s.uses: Beginners and bracelet makers who want a palette on one string, kit sellers. Entry tier, high volume.
multi-gemstone-heishi-and-designer-mix-s.carried: Smooth heishi 4 to 5mm at ; large tyre mixes, tag not read. At 33 ct per 8 inches of heishi, cost is about ; retail per 8 inch, per 16; tyre mixes per 16.
talkingPoints: the pink and teal are dyed chalcedony; the tag lists every stone.
keywords: lapis amazonite pink opal sunstone beads
multi-gemstone-heishi-and-designer-mix-s.folklore: Tradition says wearing many stones spreads their luck; tradition, not fact.
